Q001 An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during their Act phase. When can they first win as Usurper, and what happens if someone takes the title away meanwhile?
EXPECTED: At their next Wake they check victory before flipping Oathkeeper to Usurper, so cannot yet win as Usurper; if still Usurper at the following Wake they win. Losing the title prevents this; a new holder receives it Oathkeeper-side. At end of round eight an existing Usurper can win under the ordered endgame rules.
A: An Exile taking Oathkeeper during their Act cannot win at that Wake: on their next Wake the title flips to Usurper after victory checks, and they can first win at the following Wake if they still hold it. If another player takes it before then, the Exile does not win; regaining it resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the timing.
B: Taking the title during Act makes the Exile Oathkeeper-side. At their next Wake they check victory before flipping to Usurper; if still holding the title, they flip then, and can first win at the following Wake if they remain Usurper. If they lose and later retake it, it resets to Oathkeeper, restarting the sequence.

Q002 List all four Oaths, their matching Visions, and the extra universal requirement for a Visionary win. Do ties for most count for a Vision?
EXPECTED: Supremacy/Conquest: most sites; People/Rebellion: People’s Favor; Protection/Sanctuary: most relics and banners combined; Devotion/Faith: Darkest Secret. Exile must have the Vision revealed, fulfill it at Wake (or the round-eight check), and at least three Visions must have been drawn from the world deck. Most means strictly more than every other player, not a tie.
A: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary win also requires an Exile to have that true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck. For Conquest and Sanctuary, 'most' means strictly more than every other player, so a tie does not count.
B: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary requires an Exile to have a revealed true Vision, complete its goal at Wake, and have at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck. For Conquest/Sanctuary, ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player, so a tie does not qualify.

Q003 When are end dice rolled, what results end the game, and can an Exile Oathkeeper permit such a roll?
EXPECTED: Only at end of rounds five/six/seven with Chancellor or Citizen Oathkeeper: 6 / 5–6 / 3–6 respectively. Exile Oathkeeper prevents the roll. Eighth round ends automatically.
A: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, and 3–6 in round 7. Chancellor wins unless a Citizen meets the Successor goal, in which case that Citizen wins alone. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll.
B: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll only if Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7; otherwise continue. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll. An Exile Oathkeeper cannot permit it.

Q004 At round eight, what is the complete victory priority including simultaneous Visions and Citizens?
EXPECTED: Empire if Chancellor/Citizen Oathkeeper, then Exile Usurper, then qualifying Exile Visionary (Conquest > Rebellion > Sanctuary > Faith), then Empire fallback. Each Empire win is Chancellor unless a Citizen fulfills the Successor goal, who wins alone instead.
A: At round 8, check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualified Citizen Successor replacing the Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions ordered Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again with a qualified Citizen Successor replacing the Chancellor. A Citizen does not qualify by a Vision or Usurper status.
B: At round 8: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualified Citizen Successor winning alone instead of the Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifiers resolved Conquest, then Rebellion, then Sanctuary, then Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again with a qualified Successor replacing the Chancellor. An Exile being Oathkeeper alone does not prevent the final Empire fallback.

Q005 Give the Successor goal for each Oath. May a Citizen win by a revealed Vision or becoming Usurper?
EXPECTED: Supremacy: more relics+banners than Chancellor and every other Citizen; People: Darkest Secret; Protection: People’s Favor; Devotion: Grand Scepter. Citizens do not win by Usurper or Vision, only replace a Chancellor win via succession.
A: Supremacy: hold more relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by a revealed Vision or by becoming Usurper; Citizens cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.
B: Supremacy Successor: hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by revealing a true Vision or becoming Usurper.

Q006 Resolve the People’s Favor at Wake, including the Mob side, its last favor, and when the Mob threshold is checked.
EXPECTED: First choose to put one board favor on it or move one from it to least-full bank (choose ties); it cannot lose its last favor, so at one must add if able, otherwise nothing. Repeat that step once if already Mob. After these steps flip to Mob if six or more favor. Then check Exile wins, flip Oathkeeper, and resolve optional opportunity-site income.
A: At Wake, if holding People's Favor, either place 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank (choose among ties). Do not remove its last favor: if it has one, add one if able, otherwise do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After the choice(s), flip it to Mob if it has at least 6 favor. If it becomes Mob at that final check, there is no retroactive extra payment that Wake.
B: At Wake, if holding People's Favor, either add 1 favor from your board to it or return 1 from it to the least-full suit bank, choosing among ties. Never remove its last favor: with one favor you must add if able; if you have none, do nothing. On the Mob side, repeat that choice once. After these steps, flip it to Mob if it has 6 or more favor. Reaching the Mob threshold at this final check does not cause a second payment that Wake.

Q007 What happens in Rest, in order, and how do Citizen Supply and saved Supply work?
EXPECTED: Return favor from denizens/edifices to matching banks; secrets from denizens/edifices/relics to acting board and flip own facedown secrets up; Exile/Chancellor refresh to personal-bank-warband space, Citizen to exact Chancellor marker space including leftmost; add remaining unspent Supply by moving left, capped at leftmost; optional Rest powers once each any order.
A: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply; save unspent Supply; then take optional Rest powers once each in any chosen order. Exiles and Chancellor refresh according to warbands in their personal bank. Citizens refresh to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost. For each unspent Supply, move the marker one extra space left, capped at leftmost (7 Supply).
B: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown board secrets faceup; refresh Supply; save remaining unspent Supply by moving one extra space left per unused Supply, capped at the leftmost space; then optional Rest powers once each in chosen order. Chancellor/Exile refresh according to their warbands remaining in personal bank; Citizens refresh to the exact Chancellor marker space, including the leftmost. Thus saved Supply affects next Supply through its leftward movement.

Q008 Explain Search sources/costs and how drawing a Vision differs between world deck and discard pile.
EXPECTED: Choose only world deck or own-region discard, 2 Supply for discard, world cost 2 at zero Visions, 3 at one/two, 4 at three–five, modified by powers (Darkest Secret makes world draw 2). Draw up to three available; from world one at a time, announce a Vision, stop immediately and increment track; discard Vision does neither. Discard all but one before playing or discarding that one.
A: Search uses either the world deck or the discard pile for the pawn's region, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 with zero Visions drawn, 3 with 1–2, or 4 with 3–5; Darkest Secret makes that world-deck cost 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw up to 3. In the world deck, draw one at a time and stop immediately when a Vision appears, announcing it and advancing the Visions Drawn track by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop the draw or advance the track.
B: Search either the world deck or the discard pile for the pawn's region, never both. A discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. A world-deck Search costs 2 at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret changes the world-deck cost to 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw up to 3. From the world deck, drawing a Vision is announced, immediately ends that draw, and advances Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop drawing or advance the track.

Q009 Where do discarded cards and resources on them go, including a card at a remote site?
EXPECTED: Facedown atop next-region pile: Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle, acting player chooses order. Base on pawn region for drawn/adviser cards; if discarding a card in a different region, use that card’s region. Favor immediately goes to matching bank; secrets to acting board facedown.
A: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle. Cards from hand/advisers use your pawn's region; a card discarded from a site elsewhere uses that card's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank, and secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
B: Discard cards facedown on the next region's discard pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle. Cards from hand/advisers use the player's pawn region; a card discarded from a site in another region goes to the pile based on that card's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching suit bank; secrets on it go facedown to the acting player's board.

Q010 How do adviser limits, facedown restrictions, revealing later, and replacing a true Vision work?
EXPECTED: Three advisers including facedown; facedown has no suit/banner/power, any card can be held thus. Before playing over limit discard an adviser, respecting locks and any new changed limit. Minor action may play facedown adviser faceup as searched (site/advisers/revealed Vision as legal) or discard it. True faceup Vision only Exile revealed slot, not adviser, replaces/discards existing Vision. Cannot simply discard faceup adviser at will.
A: You may have up to 3 advisers total, faceup and facedown combined; discard one before exceeding the limit. Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card—including a site-only card or Vision—may be held facedown. A facedown adviser can later be played faceup as a minor action, following the rules for finishing Search, including destination/restrictions and applicable effects; it is not an unrestricted flip. A true Vision is revealed faceup in an Exile's separate Revealed Vision space, does not use an adviser slot, and replacing it with another true Vision discards the old one.
B: There may be up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown; before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser. Faceup advisers cannot normally be discarded voluntarily later without a rule allowing it. Facedown cards have no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card—including a Vision or site-only card—may be held facedown. An Exile may play a true Vision faceup into the separate Revealed Vision space; it is not an adviser and replaces/discards the old revealed Vision. Chancellor and Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them. A facedown adviser can be played faceup later as a minor action under Search play rules, or discarded.

Q011 What are Muster and both Trade costs, eligible cards, gains, destinations, and limitations when no advisers match?
EXPECTED: Only empty denizen/intact edifice at pawn site, no favor/secrets; not relic/ruin. Muster 1 Supply+one favor on card → two personal-bank warbands to board, purple for Citizen. Trade 1 Supply; one secret on card → one favor+one per matching faceup adviser from matching bank; or two favor on card → one shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser (zero if none). Finite source shortfall gives as much as possible.
A: Muster costs 1 Supply: place 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site, then gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board (Citizens gain purple). Ruins, relics, and cards already holding favor/secrets are ineligible; ruling is not required, but remote sites cannot be used. Trade also costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. Pay 1 secret to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from the card's suit bank; or put 2 favor on the card to gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers never match. With no matching adviser, the second Trade still costs 2 favor and gives zero secrets. Gains are limited by finite sources, except secrets are unlimited.
B: Muster costs 1 Supply: place 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (it must have no favor or secrets), then take 2 warbands from personal bank to your board; Citizens take purple. Relics and ruins are ineligible; you need not rule the site, and a remote site you rule cannot be used. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. Either place 1 secret to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank, or place 2 favor to gain 1 secret per matching faceup adviser from the shared bank. Facedown advisers do not match; with no matches the second option gains zero secrets, though its cost is still paid. Gains are limited by finite source supply (secrets are unlimited).

Q012 How do you Recover a relic versus either banner, and what happens to the old banner resources?
EXPECTED: 1 Supply; facedown relic at pawn site only at printed site cost, then take faceup personal bank. Either banner from anywhere, even yourself: pay more favor/secrets than old amount, stack new payment. People’s Favor flips off Mob and old favor distributes singly along banks away from deck from any starting suit wrapping. Darkest Secret: take one old secret, previous holder gets rest (self gets all; bank remainder stays bank).
A: Recover costs 1 Supply. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost, then hold it faceup in your personal bank. You cannot recover a player-held relic or a Reliquary relic. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank, by paying strictly more of its resource than it currently has. For People's Favor, place the paid favor on it and distribute its old favor singly among suit banks in the specified order; flip it to normal side if Mob, and there is no seizure penalty for Recover. For Darkest Secret, place the new secrets on it; the new holder takes one old secret and the previous holder takes the rest. If recovering from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from the shared bank, the remainder stays there.
B: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost, then hold it faceup in your personal bank. Player-held and Reliquary relics cannot be recovered. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently holds; put the payment on it, distribute its old favor one at a time through the suit banks starting anywhere and moving away from the world deck (wrapping), and flip it to normal if Mob. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds; the new holder takes 1 old secret, and the previous holder takes the rest. Recovering it from yourself returns all old secrets to you; from the shared bank, the remainder stays there. Recovering a banner has no seizure penalty.

Q013 When is another player’s Darkest Secret safe or recoverable? Include no advisers, no cards, and a ruin-only site.
EXPECTED: Recoverable if at least one suited card at holder’s pawn site matches none of their faceup advisers; no faceup advisers does not protect it if suited card exists. Empty/ruin-only site protects it; ignore suits absent on ruins/facedown advisers. Can recover from self or shared bank freely, still paying cost.
A: Another player's Darkest Secret is recoverable only if there is a suited card at their pawn's site whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers. An empty site or a ruin-only site protects it because neither supplies a suited card. Facedown advisers do not match suits. If the holder has no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, it is recoverable. Recovering your own or the shared-bank Darkest Secret ignores this protection.
B: To recover another player's Darkest Secret, their pawn's site must have a suited card that matches none of their faceup advisers. If they have no faceup advisers but there is a suited site card, it is recoverable. If they have no suited site card—an empty site or ruin-only site—it is protected. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. The protection does not apply when recovering from yourself or the shared bank.

Q014 Explain legal Campaign defender and target selection, including remote sites and a same-site relic target.
EXPECTED: 2 Supply; defender another player ruling pawn site or whose pawn there, or bandits if no player rules it. At least one target at pawn site; if defender rules it must target it. May target any defender sites anywhere; relics/banners or pawn+favor only if their pawn is at attacker site. Relic target of co-located defender satisfies local target requirement. Pawn+favor adds two defense dice; sites one each; relic printed shields; banners resource count.
A: Choose as defender another player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. Declare at least one target at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, it must be targeted. You may add any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map, each adding one defense die. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (one die per resource on the banner), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice). A relic at the shared site can itself satisfy the local-target requirement.
B: Choose another player who rules your site or whose pawn is there; if no player rules your site, bandits may be chosen. Declare at least one target at your pawn's site, and if the defender rules that site you must target it. You may also target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics, their banners, or their pawn together with their favor. A co-located defender's relic target itself satisfies the local-target requirement.

Q015 How are Campaign attack/defense calculated, and how do skulls, hollow swords, ties and sacrifices work?
EXPECTED: Attacker chooses up to board-force warbands worth of attack dice. Defense shields multiplied by each double (x2,x4,...), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board if pawn at attacker or targeted site; bandits one per targeted site. Attack skulls kill own force immediately; paired hollow swords count one, lone hollow zero. Attack must strictly exceed defense; may sacrifice force warbands +1 each, exactly enough to win, no excess; if unable/decline defender wins.
A: The attacker may roll up to as many attack dice as warbands in their attacking force. Defense is shields rolled (each double-symbol doubles shields, with multipliers stacking), plus defending warbands at targeted sites and the defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site; bandits add one per targeted bandit site. Doubles multiply shields only. Each attack skull immediately kills one warband from the attacker's own force. Count full swords; every pair of hollow swords adds one, and a leftover hollow sword adds zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing, must sacrifice exactly enough to win and cannot sacrifice extra. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie is a defender win.
B: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force. Defense is shields rolled (each double-symbol doubles shields, multipliers stack), plus defending warbands at targeted sites, plus defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's own force warbands. Count full swords, and each pair of hollow swords adds 1 (a leftover hollow sword adds nothing). The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra. The attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower means defender wins.

Q016 After an attacker wins, resolve defeat and all targets, including choosing zero garrisons, banner seizure, and banishment.
EXPECTED: Defeated force kills half rounded down; remaining returns to board; defeated effects. Attacker may move any number including zero from force onto targeted sites, takes all targeted relics/banners; seized banners burn two resources to min one, People’s Favor becomes Mob. If pawn+favor targeted may banish to legal chosen site for no Supply and may burn half favor rounded down. Shrouded Wood can override destination. Victory effects then end-discard plans.
A: The defeated side kills half its remaining force, rounded down, and returns survivors to its board; bandits cannot be killed and hide. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. If the attacker wins, they may place any number of surviving force warbands—including zero—on any targeted sites. With zero placed, a site is left to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners; a seized banner (other than one taken by Recover) loses 2 resources, down to at least 1, and People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Resolve victorious battle-plan effects and end-of-Campaign plan discards; transfer Supremacy title at the end of Campaign.
B: After the roll, the defeated side kills half its remaining force, rounded down, and returns survivors to its board; bandits cannot be killed and hide. If the attacker wins, they may place any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites; zero leaves the site to bandits unless another power applies. They take all targeted relics and banners. A banner seized by Campaign (or otherwise taken outside Recover) loses 2 resources down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site without Supply, and separately may burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Site travel restrictions such as Shrouded Wood still apply.

Q017 What changes in a Campaign involving Imperial defenders or a Citizen attacking another Imperial player?
EXPECTED: Citizen attacker against Chancellor/Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; Citizen targeted by Chancellor likewise. Imperial defender gets Chancellor automatically as Ally; non-attacker Citizens may join with permission if pawn at targeted site or attacker site. Activate defender/allies modifiers, share side powers and battle plans, one use per plan paid by user, never another’s advisers; qualifying allied board warbands defend. Chancellor chooses losses; survivors at sites go Chancellor board, Citizens keep own board survivors. Declared defender decides contested timing/order. Oathkeeper defense bonus shared even non-Supremacy.
A: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally; other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. The defending side shares the applicable title defense bonus, even outside Supremacy, and activates modifiers ruled by the defender or Allies. Allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. Defenders/Allies can use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers; the defender decides contested timing and shared-power use, and the Chancellor chooses Imperial warband losses. When a Citizen attacks Chancellor or another Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make every Citizen non-Imperial.
B: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. Defender and Allies activate their relevant Campaign modifiers; the title's defense bonus is shared by the defending side, and allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. They may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not another player's advisers; a player pays for their own plan and the same plan cannot be shared. The specified temporary non-Imperial cases are: a Citizen attacking the Chancellor or another Citizen, or the Chancellor attacking a Citizen. In an intra-Empire Campaign, only the specified attacker/defender loses Imperial status for that Campaign, not every Citizen.

Q018 State all base Travel costs and what happens when a facedown destination is revealed. How do fixed costs, increases and free Travel interact?
EXPECTED: Cradle→Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; Provinces→any other site 2; Hinterland→Hinterland 3, Provinces 2, Cradle 4. Move pawn, reveal site and add printed favor/secrets from shared bank and facedown relics from relic deck. Apply fixed-number Travel cost first then other modifiers; spend-no-Supply overrides all increases. Pawn movement does not move site warbands.
A: Base Travel costs by origin/destination region are: Cradle to Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; Provinces to Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland 2; Hinterland to Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel to a facedown site reveals it and places its printed favor/secrets there and its printed relics facedown beside it. Apply fixed-number Travel costs first, then other increases/decreases. A modifier that says spend no Supply overrides all cost increases. Site-entry restrictions apply unless explicitly ignored; site powers can also change costs and restrictions.
B: Base Travel costs by origin/destination region are: from Cradle, 1 to Cradle, 2 to Provinces, 4 to Hinterland; from Provinces, 2 to each region; from Hinterland, 4 to Cradle, 2 to Provinces, 3 to Hinterland. The destination may be any different site, not just an adjacent one. A facedown destination is revealed and gets its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and printed number of facedown relics from the relic deck. Apply fixed-number Travel costs first, then other increases/decreases. A modifier saying ‘spend no Supply’ overrides all cost increases; site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by name or power.

Q019 How can Citizenship be offered and accepted during play, and what may or must be exchanged?
EXPECTED: Grand Scepter holder (not taken this turn) offers any Exile including self exactly one Reliquary relic plus optional binding exchange favor,secrets,banners,non-Reliquary relics. Accepted: flip Citizen, replace all board/map warbands purple as available with recipient choosing shortfall removals/replacements, discard revealed Vision, Usurper→Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, refresh full. Exchange agreed items; Chancellor gains uncovered mandatory modifier. All Imperials rule purple sites. Reliquary relics inaccessible to Campaign/Recover, powers unusable, do not count goals.
A: The Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, or exile another Citizen; the Scepter's powers cannot be used on the turn it was taken. A normal offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic, and may also negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics; the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. Acceptance flips the recipient to Citizen, replaces their board/map warbands with purple (choosing removals if purple is insufficient), discards their revealed Vision, flips Usurper to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if it is their turn, refreshes to full Supply, exchanges the promised pieces, and gives the Chancellor the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers apply acceptance without a negotiated offer.
B: The Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, or exile another Citizen; the Scepter's powers cannot be used on the turn it was taken. A Citizenship offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic, and may negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics; the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, flip to Citizen, replace all own warbands on board/map with purple (choosing removals if purple is insufficient), discard a revealed Vision, flip Usurper to Oathkeeper, end the recipient's Act if it is their turn, and refresh to full Supply. Exchange the promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced-Citizenship powers bypass negotiation. Separately, a Citizen without the Scepter may self-exile by giving the Scepter holder favor equal to own board warbands plus their secrets on board and on denizen/relic/edifice cards; they cannot do this while holding the Scepter, and it ends their Act. Exiling another Citizen has a specified favor payment, makes them Exile and replaces their board purple warbands; map garrisons remain purple.

Q020 Describe the Chronicle’s new Oath choice, Citizenship turnover, and world-deck rebuilding, including why the top stack is not 14 cards.
EXPECTED: Vision-only winner uses matching Oath; other/multiple-method win chooses any different Oath. Exile winner flips all Citizens even boxed to Exile then may offer other Exiles except newly flipped; accepted map garrisons replaced one each by winner warband (ignore normal offer). Rebuild remaining denizens: ten+two random Visions=12 top, fifteen+three Visions=18 middle, remaining denizens bottom. Chronicle aid 12 denizens+2 is erroneous.
A: After a Vision-only victory, the next Oath must match that Vision; after any other victory or multiple victory methods, choose any Oath except the current one. If the winner is an Exile, turn all Citizen boards—including boxed boards—to Exile; they may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped, but not themself. To rebuild the world deck, shuffle denizens remaining in play (excluding those at sites, in the Archive, or Dispossessed), then make a top stack of 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 total), a middle stack of 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 total), and put remaining denizens below. The top stack is not 14 because the Chronicle aid's '12 denizens + 2' is identified as incorrect; the specified composition is 10 + 2.
B: A victory by Vision alone sets the next Oath to match that Vision. Any other victory, including multiple victory methods, allows any Oath except the current one. If the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards—including boxed boards—to Exile; the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped, with normal offer cost/relic rules ignored, but cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship. For rebuilding the world deck, shuffle remaining in-play denizens; put 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards total) on top, then 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), with remaining denizens below. The Chronicle aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ is incorrect; that would make a 14-card top stack, so it is 10 denizens + 2 Visions.
"}

2:title: "Oath: Chronicles of Empire and Exile"
3:bgg_id: 291572
4:player_count: "2–6 (multiplayer rules; no automated opponent)"
5:play_time: "45–150 minutes"
6:designer: "Cole Wehrle"
7:source_pdf: "https://buriedgiant.com/oath/Oath_Law_of_Oath.pdf"
8:extracted_date: "2026-11-05"
9:summarized_date: "2026-11-05"
10:rulebook_version: "2021 base game first printing: Law dated October 20, 2020 and corresponding Playbook; official base-game errata updated November 15, 2022"
11:verification: unverified
12:verification_date: null
13:---
14:
15:## Overview
16:
17:One player is the Chancellor; the others are Exiles or Citizens. Players compete for a changing Oath, personal Visions, or succession to the Chancellor. One player wins alone. After victory, the winner writes the Chronicle, preserving a changed map, population of cards, and political order for the next game. New players can join later games.
18:
19:This summary covers the complete multiplayer base game, first-game and later-game setup, and Chronicle. It incorporates the official first-printing clarifications, particularly the corrected Darkest Secret recovery restriction and Imperial defense sharing. It excludes the Clockwork Prince and New Foundations. The Law governs over the Playbook and aids except the Site Reference; printed card powers and the rules hierarchy below apply.
20:
21:## Components
22:
23:Map with Cradle (2 sites), Provinces (3), Hinterland (3), a facedown discard pile per region, six suit favor banks, round track, Visions Drawn track, world deck and relic deck. The game contains 23 sites, 198 denizens, 5 Visions (4 true Visions and the Conspiracy), 6 double-sided edifices, 20 relics plus the Grand Scepter, 2 banners, 4 goal references, Chancellor board, 5 Exile/Citizen boards, Imperial Reliquary, 6 pawns, 94 warbands (24 purple; 14 in each other color), 36 favor, 20 secret tokens, 10 attack dice, 6 defense dice, an end die, markers and aids. The Archive holds denizens by suit and the Dispossessed; the World Box saves the map and goal.
24:
25:Your **board** holds resources and your mobile warband force. Your **personal bank** beside it holds unused warbands and held relics/banners. Your **advisers** are up to three cards to its right, counting both faceup and facedown. A revealed true Vision occupies an Exile's separate Revealed Vision space and does not use an adviser slot.
26:
27:A player's pawn determines **your site** and **your region**. A pawn does not rule a site. You rule each faceup site containing your warbands, the cards at those sites, and your advisers. Sites hold only one color of warbands. All Imperial players rule every purple-garrisoned site. Bandits rule faceup sites without physical warbands; they are enemies to all players and do not compete for victory. Facedown sites cannot hold cards or be ruled.
28:
29:Denizen suits are Discord, Arcane, Order, Hearth, Beast, Nomad, in that clockwise favor-bank order. A site shows its denizen/edifice card capacity, reveal prompt, relic Recover cost and special power. Both intact and ruined edifices use capacity; a ruin has no suit and cannot be used for Muster or Trade. Relics beside sites do not use their denizen/edifice capacity.
30:
31:## Setup
32:
33:### First game: preserve the packet order
34:
35:Use packets A, B and C and the Playbook's setup, preferably with four players (Chancellor, then Red, Blue, Yellow clockwise). Do not shuffle the prepared first-game decks. The packet-based one-round walkthrough is optional teaching guidance; play afterwards uses the full rules here.
36:
37:1. Lay out the map. Put Plains faceup in top Cradle slot, Mountain faceup in top Provinces slot, Rocky Coast faceup in top Hinterland slot. Place the other five packet sites facedown in their marked order: Lush Coast in the other Cradle slot, Wastes in middle Hinterland, Salt Flats in bottom Provinces; preserve the other packet placements.
38:2. Put purple pawn on Plains, Red and Blue on Mountain, Yellow on Rocky Coast. Place 2 purple warbands on Plains and 1 each on Mountain and Rocky Coast.
39:3. Start round and Visions Drawn markers on their starred spaces (round 1, zero Visions). Use Oathkeeper of Supremacy. Place banners in shared bank, People's Favor normal side with 1 favor, Darkest Secret with 1 secret. Put 3 favor in each suit bank; collect remaining favor, secrets and dice in shared bank.
40:4. Chancellor takes Chancellor board, Reliquary and Grand Scepter, 3 purple warbands on board and 17 in personal bank (4 are already on map), 2 favor and 1 secret on board, full leftmost Supply, and Oathkeeper title. Each Exile has 3 of their 14 warbands on board, 11 in personal bank, 1 favor, 1 secret, and full Supply.
41:5. Place Longbows on Plains, Taming Charm on Mountain, Elders on Rocky Coast. Seed Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland discard piles with 3/3/5 cards from the ordered packet. Give facedown advisers: Chancellor Forest Paths; Red Animal Playmates; Blue Naysayers; Yellow A Small Favor. Put remaining 41 denizen/Vision cards from packet B, still ordered, in world deck.
42:6. Place Ivory Eye facedown at Mountain, next 4 packet relics facedown on Reliquary spaces, remaining 15 in relic deck. Begin Chancellor's turn. The four-player walkthrough can be followed with three people by one person handling two colors; after the walkthrough remove one Exile color's pieces and discard their cards to continue with three.
43:
44:### Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)
45:
46:1. Deal saved sites with attached denizens, edifices and relics to map slots: Cradle fully, then Provinces, then Hinterland, top to bottom. Start round 1 and Visions Drawn 0; use saved goal reference.
47:2. Collect shared pieces and both banners. People's Favor begins normal side with 1 favor; Darkest Secret has 1 secret. Put **3 favor per suit bank**, or **4 each with 5–6 players**.
48:3. Choose Chancellor (previous winner recommended), seated at Cradle, others randomly. Chancellor takes purple pieces, board, Reliquary and Grand Scepter. Other players in turn order choose a board on its saved Exile or Citizen side and corresponding color's pieces. Starting Citizens receive no Reliquary relic.
49:4. All start at full leftmost Supply. Chancellor has 2 favor, 1 secret and 3 purple warbands on board; place 2 purple warbands on topmost faceup Cradle site and 1 at each other faceup site with a denizen or intact edifice. Chancellor begins as Oathkeeper; additionally takes Darkest Secret for Devotion or People's Favor for People.
50:5. Each Exile/Citizen has 1 favor and 1 secret on board; Exiles have 3 own-color board warbands, Citizens 3 purple board warbands. Resolve printed site favor/secret setup prompts from shared bank; if insufficient favor Chancellor chooses allocation. Existing Chronicled site relics stay with sites.
51:6. Draw 4 relics and place them randomly, one facedown on each Reliquary space; put remaining relics in relic deck.
52:7. If world deck was not rebuilt during previous Chronicle, first form its top 12 cards from **10 denizens plus 2 random Visions**, its next 18 from **15 denizens plus remaining 3 Visions**, and remaining denizens below. Otherwise keep the saved rebuilt deck.
53:8. Take 3 total cards from bottom of world deck, one per region discard. Each player in turn order draws 3 from bottom of world deck. Advance Visions Drawn for any Visions drawn. Starting Chancellor, each player places pawn on any faceup site (Chancellor must choose top Cradle site), chooses 1 drawn card as facedown adviser, and discards other 2 using normal regional destinations. Put remaining world deck on map.
54:
55:## Turn Structure
56:
57:Play clockwise from Chancellor, one turn each per round, for at most eight rounds. Each turn is **Wake → Act → Rest**. After everyone has acted, check round-end victory and advance round marker if play continues.
58:
59:### Wake: mandatory order
60:
61:1. **People's Favor**, if held: either put 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Never remove its last favor: at 1, you must add if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If banner is already Mob-side, repeat this choice once. Afterwards, if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob. A banner becoming Mob at this last step does not retroactively repeat the payment that Wake.
62:2. If Exile, check Usurper and Visionary wins.
63:3. If Exile holding Oathkeeper title, flip it to Usurper. Victory was checked **before** this flip.
64:4. At Salt Flats, Mine or Drowned City, optionally take 1 favor or secret from that site.
65:
66:### Act
67:
68:Take any number of major actions, minor actions and Action powers, in any order, including repeating or taking none, provided you pay each cost. Finish an action before starting another. Spend Supply by moving marker right one space per point. Minor actions use no Supply but may have resource costs.
69:
70:### Rest: mandatory order
71:
72:1. Return favor on denizens/edifices to suit-matching banks.
73:2. Return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board. Flip facedown secrets on your board faceup.
74:3. Exile/Chancellor refresh Supply to the space showing their warbands remaining in personal bank. For Chancellor: 18+ gives 6 Supply, 11–17 gives 5, 4–10 gives 4, 0–3 gives 3. For Exile: 9+ gives 6, 4–8 gives 5, 0–3 gives 4. Citizen refreshes to the **exact Chancellor marker space**, including leftmost, not by counting purple warbands.
75:4. Save remaining unspent Supply: move marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply).
76:5. Optional Rest powers, each once in chosen order.
77:
78:## Actions
79:
80:### Search — 2–4 Supply
81:
82:Choose either world deck or your pawn's region discard pile, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces the world-deck cost with 2. Other applicable modifiers still apply.
83:
84:Draw up to 3 available cards. From world deck, draw one at a time: if a Vision is drawn, announce that fact, **stop immediately** and increase Visions Drawn by 1. Drawing Visions from a discard does not stop drawing or advance the track. If source empties, draw only what remains; no reshuffle is implied.
85:
86:Discard all but 1 drawn card **before** playing the remaining card, or discard that last card too. Options:
87:
88:- **Site:** play faceup at your pawn's site, only below its denizen/edifice capacity. Gain 1 favor from that card's suit bank. With People's Favor you may first discard a card from any site in your region, then play to any site in your region, subject to locks and capacity; discarded and receiving sites can differ.
89:- **Adviser:** play faceup or facedown. Up to 3 total, including facedown; before exceeding limit discard an adviser. Faceup advisers cannot be discarded voluntarily at other times without a rule permitting it. Facedown cards have no suit, restriction banner or power; any card, including site-only cards and Visions, can be held facedown.
90:- **True Vision:** Exile only, faceup in Revealed Vision slot, replacing and discarding old revealed Vision. Not an adviser. Chancellor/Citizens can hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
91:
92:**Discard destinations:** facedown atop next region's pile: Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle, ordering multiple discards as you choose. For cards in hand/advisers use your pawn's region; when discarding a card at a site in another region, use the card's region. Favor on discarded cards immediately returns to matching bank; their secrets go to acting player's board **facedown**.
93:
94:**Conspiracy:** anyone may play it faceup; it does not replace a true Vision. You may burn 1 secret to take 1 relic or banner from a player whose pawn is at your site, if at least 2 of your faceup advisers match the suit of any of their advisers. Both of yours can match the same single adviser of theirs. Apply banner seizure penalty. Then return Conspiracy to box, even if no theft was made.
95:
96:### Muster — 1 Supply
97:
98:Place 1 favor on an **empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site** (no favor or secrets already). Gain 2 warbands from personal bank onto board; Citizens gain purple. Relics/ruins are ineligible. Rule is not required, and ruling a remote site does not allow remote Muster.
99:
100:### Trade — 1 Supply
101:
102:Choose an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site; no relics/ruins. Choose:
103:
104:- Put 1 secret on card: gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser, from that card's suit bank.
105:- Put 2 favor on card: gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. With no matching advisers gain **zero** secrets.
106:
107:Facedown advisers never match. Finite source exhaustion gives only available favor/warbands; secrets are unlimited. Costs remain payable even if a gain is reduced to zero.
108:
109:### Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost
110:
111:Recover 1 **facedown relic at your site** or either banner from anywhere, including yourself or shared bank. Relics held by players or in Reliquary cannot be recovered. Pay relic's site cost (3 favor to indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in personal bank. You may hold unlimited relics/banners and peek before choosing.
112:
113:- **People's Favor:** pay any amount of favor strictly greater than its current favor. Put paid favor on banner; distribute old favor singly to suit banks, starting anywhere and moving away from world deck through banks, wrapping. Flip it to normal side if Mob. No seizure penalty when recovering.
114:- **Darkest Secret:** pay any amount of secrets strictly greater than current secrets. Put paid secrets on it; new holder takes 1 old secret, previous holder takes rest. Recovering from self returns all old secrets to yourself; from shared bank, remainder stays in bank.
115:
116:**Darkest Secret protection, corrected by official errata:** to recover from another player, there must be a **suited card at their pawn's site matching none of their faceup advisers**. Empty sites and ruin-only sites protect it. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. If holder has no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, it **is recoverable**; the printed Law's contrary parenthetical is erroneous. Recovering from self or shared bank ignores this protection.
117:
118:### Campaign — 2 Supply
119:
120:Resolve all steps in order. Your **force** normally means board warbands for attacker, and all warbands contributing to defense for defender.
121:
122:1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
123:2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2.
124:3. **Battle plans:** attacker chooses ruled plans once each, then defender. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
125:4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
126:5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
127:6. **Resolve defeat:** defeated side kills half its remaining force, rounded down, and returns survivors to board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.
128:7. **If attacker won:** may place any number, including **zero**, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves site to bandits unless another power applies. Take **all** targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner (taken any way except Recover), burn 2 of its resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor targeted, may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half their board favor, rounded down. Respect site travel restrictions, notably Shrouded Wood.
129:8. Resolve victorious battle-plan effects, then any end-of-Campaign plan discards. Transfer Supremacy title **at end of Campaign**, not during temporary loss of site rule.
130:
131:**Imperial defense:** when an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with defender's permission if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Activate all Campaign modifiers ruled by defender/Allies; applicable title defense bonus is shared on the defending side even outside Supremacy. Allied board warbands add defense only if pawn at attacker site or targeted site. Defender/Allies may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, **not other players' advisers**. User pays; same plan cannot be used by multiple players. On powers, “you,” “your enemy,” “the defender,” etc. refer to the entire side, but **your site/your board** still mean that player's own pawn site/board. Declared defender decides contested timing, priority and who uses a shared power. Chancellor controls loss selection as above. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make all Citizens non-Imperial; only the specified attacker/defender loses that status temporarily.
132:
133:### Travel — 1–4 Supply before modifiers
134:
135:Move pawn to any different site, not necessarily an adjacent slot; site garrisons stay put. Board warbands travel with your pawn in the sense that they stay on your board.
136:
137:| From / to | Cradle | Provinces | Hinterland |
138:|---|---:|---:|---:|
139:| Cradle | 1 | 2 | 4 |
140:| Provinces | 2 | 2 | 2 |
141:| Hinterland | 4 | 2 | 3 |
142:
143:Reveal facedown destination; put printed favor/secrets there from shared bank and printed number of relics beside it facedown from relic deck. Apply fixed-number Travel costs first, then other increases/decreases; a modifier saying **spend no Supply** overrides all cost increases. Site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by name/power.
144:
145:### Minor actions — no Supply
146:
147:- Play a facedown adviser faceup as if just finishing Search, following destination/restrictions, site favor and When Played effects; or discard it. Not simply an unrestricted in-place flip.
148:- Use an accessible Action power; free powers may repeat unless limited, paid ones obey exhaustion.
149:- Peek at facedown relics at your site. Once you have peeked at a particular relic, you can peek again from any site. Grand Scepter holder may peek in Reliquary.
150:- Move any number of your warbands from your site to board **except the last one**. Drop board warbands only at your site **if you rule it**. Bandit sites cannot be occupied by simple drop-off. Citizen pickup requires Chancellor's permission. Imperial players with pawns together may give/take board warbands from each other with recipient/other player's permission.
151:
152:### Citizenship and exile during play
153:
154:**Grand Scepter:** cannot use its powers the turn you took it. Its holder, even an Exile, may offer Citizenship to any Exile **including themself**, or exile another Citizen. Reliquary relics cannot be campaigned/recovered, their powers cannot be used, and they do not count toward goals while there.
155:
156:**Offer:** must promise **exactly one Reliquary relic**; may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners and non-Reliquary relics. May let recipient peek at Reliquary relics. Other binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics.
157:
158:**Acceptance:** flip to Citizen; replace all own warbands on board/map with purple. If insufficient purple, new Citizen chooses which to remove and which to replace. Discard revealed Vision, flip own Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, and refresh to full leftmost Supply. Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered **mandatory** Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers apply acceptance without a negotiated offer. All Imperials rule purple sites; Citizenship does not itself grant a separate shared victory.
159:
160:**Exile another Citizen:** Scepter holder pays them 5 favor, +1 if recipient is Oathkeeper, +1 if recipient holds People's Favor, −1 if payer is Oathkeeper, −1 if payer holds People's Favor (range 3–7). Recipient flips Exile, replaces **board** purple warbands with own color and refreshes full. Purple map garrisons stay Imperial. This does not end their Act by itself.
161:
162:**Self-exile:** Citizen who does not hold Scepter may give its holder favor equal to own board warbands **plus all their secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards**. Flip Exile, replace board warbands with own color, refresh full, and **end Act**. Cannot self-exile while holding Scepter. Map garrisons stay purple.
163:
164:## Scoring / Victory Conditions
165:
166:### Oathkeeper title and four Oaths
167:
168:| Oath | Oathkeeper criterion | Matching Vision | Citizen Successor goal |
169:|---|---|---|---|
170:| Supremacy | Rule most sites | Conquest | Hold more relics+banners than Chancellor **and every other Citizen** |
171:| People | Hold People's Favor | Rebellion | Hold Darkest Secret |
172:| Protection | Hold most relics+banners combined | Sanctuary | Hold People's Favor |
173:| Devotion | Hold Darkest Secret | Faith | Hold Grand Scepter |
174:
175:Current holder keeps title on a tie for its goal. If holder no longer meets goal and several others tie for it, outgoing holder chooses recipient. A new holder always takes it Oathkeeper-side, never Usurper-side. Under Supremacy Chancellor holds it if Empire collectively meets goal; Citizens do not count purple sites separately against each other. Other Oaths concern personal holdings. The Grand Scepter counts as a relic when held; Reliquary relics do not.
176:
177:**Usurper victory:** Exile wins at Wake if already Usurper. Taking title during Act normally requires surviving to next Wake to flip, then surviving to following Wake to win. Losing and retaking title resets it to Oathkeeper. An existing Usurper may instead win at round-eight check.
178:
179:**Visionary victory:** Exile must have true Vision revealed and goal completed at Wake, with **at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck**. Can reveal it earlier but cannot win early. For Conquest/Sanctuary “most” means **strictly more than every other player**, no ties. Compare to Empire's shared rule for sites. Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.
180:
181:**Stable regime:** at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll end die only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper. Ends on respectively **6 / 5–6 / 3–6**. Chancellor wins, except a Citizen meeting Successor goal wins **alone instead**. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.
182:
183:**War exhaustion:** round 8 ends automatically. Check in this exact priority:
184:
185:1. If Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper: Empire wins (Chancellor unless qualified Successor).
186:2. Otherwise, Exile Usurper wins.
187:3. Otherwise, qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins. If several qualify, priority **Conquest → Rebellion → Sanctuary → Faith**.
188:4. Otherwise Empire wins (Chancellor unless qualified Successor), even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.
189:
190:Holding Successor goal never ends game on its own. Resolve it whenever Chancellor would win. After victory, write Chronicle below.
191:
192:## Special Rules & Edge Cases
193:
194:### Powers, costs and information
195:
196:Access a card's power if you rule it or your pawn is at its site; relic holders use held relics. Persistent powers (thick black braid) affect the players specified regardless of ordinary access. Sites specify their own use conditions. Chancellor must apply uncovered Reliquary modifiers; title holder must apply title power.
197:
198:Pay the braid/text cost. Normally cannot place favor/secrets on a card already holding either; battle-plan payment is the exception, not a license to Muster/Trade there. If power has no cost you can still use it despite existing resources. When paying outside your turn, favor goes immediately to matching bank; secrets stay on your board **facedown**. Facedown secrets cannot pay any place or burn cost until flipped up. Burn sends prompted resource to shared bank. Kill sends warband to its color's personal bank (purple to Chancellor). Sacrifice means choose to kill own warbands.
199:
200:Resolve as much of used power as possible except optional “may” parts; may pay to use a power even if its effect does nothing. Cannot give away/burn/sacrifice extra resources beyond prompted cost or amount.
201:
202:Faceup **tree** cards are site-only; **person** cards adviser-only; restrictions also govern moves/swaps. **Locked** cards cannot be discarded, moved or swapped once faceup except in Chronicle. Cards reducing adviser limit require discard based on **new limit before playing**; with multiple limit-changers use lowest, not sum. Respect locks.
203:
204:Ordinary major-action modifiers are chosen at action start, used once per action, in any order; cannot discard an active modifier during that action. No-cost modifier may be used on multiple distinct actions. Must/cannot modifiers are mandatory. Battle plans instead occur in Campaign step 3, attacker first; each once per Campaign. Wake/Rest powers occur once at their stated phase; When Played is mandatory after site favor, Homeland effects and modifiers.
205:
206:Rules priority: read literally; Law supersedes Playbook/aids except Site Reference; non-italic rules override italic reminders. “Must” overrides ordinary rules; “cannot” overrides even “must”; “ignore” overrides named must/cannot restrictions. “Must if able” has no penalty when unable. Promises are normally nonbinding, and pieces cannot simply be transferred without permission in a rule; Citizenship offers and expressly binding powers are exceptions. Tribunal disputed breach is settled by coin flip. Give and Take are distinct keywords; restricting one does not automatically restrict the other.
207:
208:Component limits: favor/warbands/cards limited to available pieces; take/gain as much as possible if source short. Secrets and dice unlimited; use multipliers or roll again if needed. Banks/boards unlimited capacity unless explicitly limited. Facedown advisers can be inspected by holder and shown to others; their identity may be discussed or lied about. Private: facedown card fronts, discard fronts, world-deck count, world-deck backs below top. Public: discard counts/backs and board-resource/warband counts, and all other information. Keep facedown advisers distinct. Playbook group agreements about undoing actions or sharing drawn hands are social options, not additional mandatory rules.
209:
210:### Site powers (Site Reference)
211:
212:- **Opportunity** (Salt Flats/Mine/Drowned City): at end of your Wake take 1 favor/secret from site, optionally.
213:- **Homeland** sites: when you play a matching-suit card there and have not discarded a card there this turn, gain printed favor from matching bank, 2 warbands, or take its relic as Recover, as shown. A relic Recover still pays normal relic cost but no Supply.
214:- **Coasts:** traveling from one Coast to another costs 1 Supply and ignores Narrow Pass.
215:- **Plains/Mountain:** must add/subtract 1 attack die when site or anything at site is targeted, even if attacker rules it.
216:- **River:** Muster there gains 1 additional warband if you rule it.
217:- **Charming Valley:** traveling from it increases Travel cost by 1.
218:- **Shrouded Wood:** travel from it costs 2, ignoring Narrow Pass and Hidden Place; if enemy rules it, travel to site of ruler's choice (Chancellor chooses for Empire), even when someone else makes you travel.
219:- **Narrow Pass:** entering its region from another must travel to it; targeting anything in its region from another region must also target it unless you rule it.
220:- **Great Slum:** when playing/moving a card there, may first discard a card there.
221:- **Marshes:** Search while pawn there draws 1 fewer card.
222:- **Buried Giant:** traveling from it may flip 1 own board secret facedown to spend no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass.
223:- **Hidden Place:** cannot travel there or declare Campaign targets there unless flipping 1 board secret facedown.
224:- **Tribunal:** Action if you rule it or pawn there: negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, relics and banners, including combined future terms and penalties.
225:
226:**Bandit Crown:** treat bandits as own warbands: rule empty faceup sites, may pick up last physical site warband, add relevant bandits to defense (or attacking force with suitable powers). Bandits themselves cannot be killed, moved or sacrificed, including skulls or battle-plan costs.
227:
228:### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)
229:
230:Winner performs these steps in order. After first game open Archive packet: place 8 dividers; put edifices in matching sections; separately shuffle each suit's denizens into its Archive section.
231:
232:1. **Vow an Oath:** won by Vision alone → next Oath matches that Vision. Any other way or multiple victory methods → choose any Oath **except current one**. Save goal in World Box.
233:2. **Citizenship:** if winner Exile, flip **all** Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile. May offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; ignore normal in-play offer cost/relic rules. Acceptors flip Citizen and replace all garrisons at sites they rule with **one winner-color warband per site**. Winner cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship.
234:3. **Map and edifices:** Imperial winner may build **or** repair **one** edifice. At ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replace denizen with matching intact Archive edifice, returning denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. Discard all sites except those winner rules or with an intact edifice; shuffle discarded sites into site deck, discard their denizens, return relics to relic deck and ruined edifices to Archive. At retained sites winner does not rule, flip intact edifice to ruin and discard all denizens there. Set aside **all sites with ruins**, with attached ruins, remaining denizens and relics, in map order top Cradle to bottom Hinterland. Remove pawns/favor/secrets/warbands from map.
235:4. **Repack map slots:** excluding set-aside ruins, fill Cradle top-down by pushing Cradle sites up then importing Provinces then Hinterland in top-down order. Fill Provinces top-down by pushing up then importing Hinterland top-down. Push Hinterland sites up. Fill empty Hinterland slots **bottom-up** with set-aside ruins **bottom-up**, then empty Provinces slots similarly. Fill any remaining slots with facedown site-deck cards; in each region with no faceup site, flip top one up.
236:5. **Add 6 denizens:** winner's most common adviser suit determines 3 random Archive cards, next clockwise suit 2, next clockwise suit 1, to world deck. Choose among tied suits; no suited advisers → choose any. Suit cycle Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord. If Archive cannot supply the full allocation, do **not** add that allocation: heal Archive instead. Sort all Dispossessed by suit; take 6 random from largest Dispossessed suit stack into world deck; shuffle remaining Dispossessed into matching Archive suit stacks.
237:6. **Dispossess 6:** set aside all 5 Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all discard piles with **losers' advisers**, move 6 random cards unseen to Dispossessed. Winner's advisers are excluded from this pool.
238:7. **Relics:** save Grand Scepter in World Box; return losing players' relics to relic deck and shuffle. Refill faceup sites with fewer relics than printed R icons up to printed number, facedown. Shuffle winner's remaining relics with Reliquary relics and stack atop relic deck.
239:8. **Save world:** stack each site's attached cards on it, stack sites so top Cradle on top and bottom Hinterland at bottom, put in World Box. Save player boards on current Exile/Citizen sides.
240:9. **Rebuild world deck:** shuffle all denizens remaining in play (not those retained at sites/Archive/Dispossessed). Top stack **10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12**; middle **15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18**; remaining denizens bottom. Save in Archive World Deck section. Chronicle aid's printed “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; do not make a 14-card top stack.
241:
242:## Player Reference
243:
244:| Action | Supply | Main additional cost/result |
245:|---|---:|---|
246:| Search | 2–4 | Up to 3 cards; world Vision stops draw; discard then play at most 1 |
247:| Muster | 1 | 1 favor on empty site card → 2 board warbands |
248:| Trade | 1 | 1 secret → 1+matching advisers favor; 2 favor → matching advisers secrets |
249:| Recover | 1 | Site relic cost or strictly outbid banner resources |
250:| Campaign | 2 | Declare local target, may add remote sites; attack must exceed defense |
251:| Travel | 1–4 | Move pawn; reveal and stock facedown site |
252:| Minor / Action power | 0 | Apply printed resource costs and permissions |
253:
254:Wake: feed People's Favor → Exile victory → flip title → opportunity site. Rest: return favor → return/ready secrets → refresh → save unspent Supply → Rest powers. End round 5/6/7: Empire Oathkeeper permits end roll 6/5–6/3–6. Round 8: Empire Oathkeeper → Usurper → Vision (Conquest/Rebellion/Sanctuary/Faith) → Empire fallback; Citizen Successor replaces any Chancellor win.
255:
256:Sources: [Law of Oath, October 20, 2020](https://buriedgiant.com/oath/Oath_Law_of_Oath.pdf), corresponding Playbook pp. 2–32, [Site Reference](https://buriedgiant.com/oath/Oath_Reference_Sheet.pdf), and [official base-game clarifications and errata, November 15, 2022](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1p2tHzbTmQhU8tPfZeK5gSJvmfScVFUeepFgIRfCpyuw/edit). Card-specific powers remain on their cards.
"}

Q005: Successor goals: under Supremacy, hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; under People, hold Darkest Secret; under Protection, hold People's Favor; under Devotion, hold Grand Scepter. Citizens/Chancellor cannot win through a true Vision or Usurper status. Holding the Successor goal alone does not end the game; it applies whenever the Chancellor would win.
Q006: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, either put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank, choosing among ties. Do not remove its last favor: if it has 1, add one if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After the choice(s), if it has 6 or more favor, flip it to Mob. Becoming Mob at this final check does not cause another repeat that Wake.
Q007: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply; save unspent Supply; then optional Rest powers, each once in chosen order. Exiles and Chancellor refresh based on warbands remaining in their personal bank, while a Citizen copies the Chancellor's exact marker space, including leftmost, rather than counting purple warbands. Saving unspent Supply moves the marker one additional space left per unspent Supply, capped at the leftmost space (7 Supply).
Q008: Search costs 2 Supply from your region discard pile. World-deck Search normally costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces that world-deck cost with 2, with other modifiers still applying. Choose either the world deck or your pawn's region discard, not both. Draw 3 unless the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it; you cannot voluntarily stop early. From the world deck, draw one at a time and stop immediately when a Vision appears, announcing it and advancing Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision from a discard pile does not stop drawing or advance the track.
Q009: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; order multiple discards as you choose. Cards from hand/advisers use your pawn's region. A card discarded from a site in another region goes to the pile based on that card's region. Favor on a discarded card returns immediately to its matching bank; secrets on it go to the acting player's board facedown.
Q010: You may have up to 3 advisers total, faceup and facedown combined. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser subject to locks. If the incoming card changes the adviser limit, check against the new limit before playing it; use the lowest of multiple limits. Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card (including site-only cards and Visions) may be held facedown. An Exile may play a true Vision faceup in the separate Revealed Vision space, replacing and discarding the old revealed Vision; it does not use an adviser slot. Chancellor and Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them. The summary does not state a specific procedure for later revealing a facedown true Vision.
Q011: Muster costs 1 Supply and places 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site, then gains 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board (purple for Citizens). Relics and ruins are ineligible; you need not rule the site, but cannot Muster remotely. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. Put 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank; or put 2 favor on it to gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers do not match; with no matching adviser, the secret trade yields zero secrets, but its cost remains payable. Gains are limited by available favor/warbands; secrets are unlimited.
Q012: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target's cost. You may take a facedown relic at your site, paying its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), or either banner from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. Relics held by players or in the Reliquary cannot be recovered. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently holds, place that payment on it, and distribute its old favor singly to suit banks starting at a chosen bank and continuing in bank order; do not return old favor to the previous holder. Flip it to normal if Mob. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds; put the payment on it, give the new holder 1 old secret and the previous holder the rest. Q013: To Recover Darkest Secret from another player, there must be a suited card at that player's pawn site matching none of their faceup advisers. Empty sites and ruin-only sites therefore protect it. If the holder has no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, it is recoverable. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. The protection does not apply when recovering it from yourself or the shared bank.
Q014: Choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may also target any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map, with one defense die per targeted site. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may additionally target any of their relics, banners, or pawn-and-favor together; a co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement.
Q015: Attacker selects up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force. Defense equals rolled shields (each double-symbol doubles shields, with multipliers stacking), plus defending warbands at targeted sites, plus defender board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site; doubles multiply shields only. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords; every pair of hollow swords adds one attack, with a lone hollow sword adding zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but must sacrifice exactly enough to win and cannot sacrifice excess. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower is a defender win.
Q016: On defeat, the defeated side kills half its remaining force, rounded down, and returns survivors to board; bandits cannot be killed and hide. If the attacker wins, they may place any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands on targeted sites. They take all targeted relics and banners. A seized banner (by any method except Recover) loses 2 resources down to a minimum of 1, and People's Favor flips to Mob. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or any target. A Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make all Citizens non-Imperial.

Apply fixed-number Travel costs first, then other increases/decreases. The summary says modifiers apply after fixed-number costs but does not give a general rule for combining a modifier that makes Travel free with other increases.

A normal offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic. It may also include a binding negotiated exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics; the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. Binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics. On acceptance, flip to Citizen and replace all own-color warbands on board/map with purple (if purple is short, the new Citizen chooses which to remove/replace); discard revealed Vision, flip Usurper to Oathkeeper, end Act if this is the recipient's turn, and refresh to full Supply. Exchange promised pieces and the Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers bypass a negotiated offer and apply acceptance directly.
Q020: If victory came solely by Vision, the next Oath matches that Vision. For any other victory or multiple victory methods, choose any Oath except the current one, and save that goal. If the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards—including boxed boards—to Exile; the winner may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting player must flip to Citizen and replace every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. The Chronicle aid's printed “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; the top stack is 12 cards, not 14.
