Favor on discarded cards immediately returns to matching bank; their secrets go to acting player's board **facedown**.
94:**Conspiracy:** anyone may play it faceup; it does not replace a true Vision. You may burn 1 secret to take 1 relic or banner from a player whose pawn is at your site, if at least 2 of your faceup advisers match the suit of any of their advisers. Both of yours can match the same single adviser of theirs. Apply banner seizure penalty. Then return Conspiracy to box, even if no theft was made.
98:Place 1 favor on an **empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site** (no favor or secrets already). Gain 2 warbands from personal bank onto board; Citizens gain purple. Relics/ruins are ineligible. Rule is not required, and ruling a remote site does not allow remote Muster.
104:- Put 1 secret on card: gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser, from that card's suit bank.
105:- Put 2 favor on card: gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. With no matching advisers gain **zero** secrets.
107:Facedown advisers never match. Finite source exhaustion gives only available favor/warbands; secrets are unlimited. Costs remain payable even if a gain is reduced to zero.
111:Recover 1 **facedown relic at your site** or either banner from anywhere, including yourself or shared bank. Relics held by players or in Reliquary cannot be recovered. Pay relic's site cost (3 favor to indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in personal bank. You may hold unlimited relics/banners and peek before choosing.
113:- **People's Favor:** pay any amount of favor strictly greater than its current favor. Put paid favor on banner; distribute old favor singly to suit banks, starting at any chosen bank, then moving away from the world deck through successive banks and wrapping as needed (the printed bank order). Do not return the old favor to the previous holder. Flip it to normal side if Mob. No seizure penalty when recovering.
114:- **Darkest Secret:** pay any amount of secrets strictly greater than current secrets. Put paid secrets on it; new holder takes 1 old secret, previous holder takes rest. Recovering from self returns all old secrets to yourself; from shared bank, remainder stays in bank.
123:2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
126:5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.

This general rule applies to all Travel, including banishment, not only named site examples. Site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by name/power.

Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered **mandatory** Reliquary modifier. **Forced Citizenship** powers apply the same status-conversion steps without a negotiated offer: no required Scepter offer or Reliquary relic gift, and no invented promised exchange. Decadent makes Provinces/Hinterland-to-Cradle Travel cost no Supply, but Travel to Hinterland costs +1. Careless gives 1 additional favor on every Trade, even when trading for secrets, but 1 fewer secret when trading for secrets. 188:**Visionary victory:** Exile must have true Vision revealed and goal completed at Wake, with **at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck by all players combined**. This is a shared global count, not a requirement for that Exile to draw three personally. Can reveal it earlier but cannot win early. For Conquest/Sanctuary “most” means **strictly more than every other player**, no ties. Compare to Empire's shared rule for sites. Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.
207:Pay the braid/text cost. Normally cannot place favor/secrets on a card already holding either; battle-plan payment is the exception, not a license to Muster/Trade there. Facedown secrets cannot pay any place or burn cost until flipped up. Burn sends prompted resource to shared bank. Kill sends warband to its color's personal bank (purple to Chancellor). Sacrifice means choose to kill own warbands.
225:- **Opportunity** (Salt Flats/Mine/Drowned City): at end of your Wake take 1 favor/secret from site, optionally.
226:- **Homeland** sites: when you play a matching-suit card there and have not discarded a card **of that same suit at that site this turn**, gain its printed reward: 1 secret from shared bank, favor from matching suit bank, 2 warbands, or take its relic treating this as Recover. 235:- **Buried Giant:** traveling from it may flip 1 own board secret facedown to spend no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass.
236:- **Hidden Place:** cannot travel there or declare Campaign targets there unless flipping 1 board secret facedown.
237:- **Tribunal:** Action if you rule it or pawn there: negotiate binding immediate exchanges of favor and secrets, as well as binding future actions in combination with any player and agreed penalties. This does not grant unrestricted immediate relic/banner transfers.
248:2. **Citizenship:** if winner Exile, flip **all** Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile. Winner cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship.
249:3. **Map and edifices:** Imperial winner may build **or** repair **one** edifice. At ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replace denizen with matching intact Archive edifice, returning denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. Discard all sites except those winner rules or with an intact edifice; shuffle discarded sites into site deck, discard their denizens, return relics to relic deck and ruined edifices to Archive. At retained sites winner does not rule, flip intact edifice to ruin and discard all denizens there. Set aside **all sites with ruins**, with attached ruins, remaining denizens and relics, in map order top Cradle to bottom Hinterland. Remove pawns/favor/secrets/warbands from map.

If it has 1 favor, you may not remove its last favor; you must add one if able, otherwise do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, make this choice twice. After the choice(s), check whether it has at least 6 favor and flip it to Mob. If it becomes Mob at this check, that does not trigger an extra payment during the same Wake.
Q007: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply; save unspent Supply; then resolve optional Rest powers, each once in chosen order. Exile/Chancellor refresh based on warbands remaining in their personal bank. Citizens refresh to exactly the Chancellor marker space, including leftmost, without counting purple warbands. Move the marker one extra space left for each unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply).
Q008: Search chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn's region, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret makes the world-deck cost 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw 3 (or fewer if source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces draws); do not voluntarily stop early. Draw from world deck one card at a time; when a Vision appears, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision in a discard pile does not stop the draw or advance the track. No reshuffle is implied when a source empties.
Q009: Discard facedown onto the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; for a hand/adviser discard, use the pile after the region of your pawn, never that same region. For a card discarded from a site in another region, use the cycle based on that card's region instead of your pawn's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
Q010: You may have up to 3 advisers total, faceup and facedown combined; before going over, discard an adviser subject to locks. If the incoming card changes the adviser limit, check the new limit before playing it; with multiple limits use the lowest. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction banner, or power; any card type, including a site-only card or Vision, can be held facedown. Later, playing or discarding a facedown adviser is a minor action; to play it faceup, use a legal destination and follow normal placement/play effects. A true Vision revealed by an Exile occupies the separate Revealed Vision space rather than an adviser slot; a newly revealed true Vision replaces and discards the old one. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them; Conspiracy can be played faceup by anyone and does not replace a true Vision.
Q011: Muster costs 1 Supply. Put 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (no favor or secrets already) and gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board; Citizens gain purple. Option A: place 1 secret on it and gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank. Option B: place 2 favor on it and gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers never match; with no matching faceup advisers, option B gains zero secrets. Gains are limited by finite favor/warband supply; secrets are unlimited, but the costs remain payable even if the gain is zero.
Q012: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. Or recover either banner from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently has; put the payment on it, distribute its old favor one at a time to suit banks in printed order starting from any chosen bank, and flip to normal if it was Mob. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it has; put payment on it, take 1 old secret for the new holder and give the rest to the previous holder (if recovering from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from shared bank, remainder stays there). No seizure penalty applies to Recover.
Q013: To recover Darkest Secret from another player, there must be at least one suited card at that player's pawn site whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. One such card is enough even if others match. If the holder has no faceup advisers, a suited site card is unmatched and the banner is recoverable. An empty site or a ruin-only site protects it because neither supplies a suited card. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. Recovery from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection.
Q014: A legal defender is any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is at your site. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may also target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map, each adding 1 defense die. If defender's pawn is at your site, you may target their relic(s) using printed defense dice, their banner(s) using dice equal to banner resources, or their pawn and favor together for 2 dice. A relic target at the shared site itself satisfies the local-target requirement.
Q015: Attacker selects up to as many attack dice as warbands in their attacking force, then applies relevant modifiers. Defense adds rolled shields (double-symbols multiply shields, stacking), all defending warbands at targeted sites, and defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords and one additional attack per pair of hollow swords; a leftover hollow sword counts zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, no excess. Attacker must strictly exceed defense; a tie means defender wins.
Q016: On attacker victory, resolve defender defeat first: defender kills half its defending-force warbands rounded down and returns the rest to board; resolve defeated-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number of surviving force warbands, including zero, on targeted sites; zero leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. Take all targeted relics/banners. A banner seized by Campaign (unlike Recover) has 2 resources burned down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, attacker may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site without Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; Shrouded Wood overrides destination choice if its enemy ruler chooses. Then resolve attacker's victorious plans. If defender wins, attacker targets are skipped and defender's victorious plans resolve. At end discard plans marked 'At end, discard.'
Q017: If an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally; other non-attacking Citizens may join with defender's permission if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. They may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not another player's advisers; each shared plan is used once total, by one user who pays, and declared defender resolves order/priority disputes. Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; surviving garrison warbands return to Chancellor's board while surviving Citizen board warbands stay there. A Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. An intra-Empire Campaign does not strip all Citizens of Imperial status.
Q018: Base Travel costs by origin-to-destination region are: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, any region 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. A facedown destination is revealed and stocked with its printed favor/secrets from shared bank and printed relic count from relic deck, facedown. Apply fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases; an applicable free-Travel power ('spend no Supply') is the final override and makes cost zero even after increases. Site entry restrictions still apply unless specifically ignored by a power.
Q019: The Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but cannot use Scepter powers on the turn they took it; they also cannot make an offer on that turn. On a later turn an offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic. They may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and may allow the recipient to peek at Reliquary relics. Acceptance flips the recipient to Citizen and replaces all their own board/map warbands with purple (if short, recipient chooses which to remove/replace), discards revealed Vision, flips their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if it is their turn, and refreshes full Supply. Forced Citizenship powers perform the conversion without an offer, relic gift, or invented exchange; only actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier. A Citizen without Scepter can self-exile by giving the Scepter holder favor equal to their board warbands plus all their secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards; they flip Exile, change board warbands to own color, refresh full, and end Act. A Scepter-holding Citizen cannot self-exile.
Q020: For the next Oath, a victory by Vision alone sets the next Oath to the one matching that Vision. Any other victory or multiple victory methods lets the winner choose any Oath except the current one. For Chronicle Citizenship, if the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards, including boxed ones, to Exile; the winner may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped, but not themself. Each accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband, regardless of previous garrison size. To rebuild the world deck, shuffle denizens remaining in play; the top stack is 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards), the middle is 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), and the remaining denizens go below. Thus it is not 14 cards: the aid's printed '12 denizens + 2' is explicitly incorrect.
"}

Q021 In later-game setup with five players, how much favor goes in each bank, what is on the banners, and what resources and warbands start on each kind of player board?
KEY Four favor per suit bank (three with two–four players). People’s Favor normal with one favor, Darkest Secret one secret. Chancellor two favor,one secret,three purple board warbands; other players one favor,one secret,three board warbands (own color Exile,purple Citizen). All full Supply.
SOURCE Law 1.4–15

Q022 How is the Chronicled map dealt, where are starting Imperial garrisons placed, and which sites receive favor/secrets during later-game setup?
KEY Deal saved sites/attached cards Cradle then Provinces then Hinterland top-down. Two purple at topmost faceup Cradle, one at each other faceup site with denizen or intact edifice; ruin alone insufficient. Put printed favor/secrets on prompted sites from bank; Chancellor allocates insufficient favor.
SOURCE Law 1.1,1.12,1.16

Q023 May later-game players choose a Citizen board or any pawn location? Does starting Citizen receive a relic, and who starts with a banner/title?
KEY Non-Chancellors choose in turn order among boards on saved sides, so Citizen only if saved Citizen. No starting relic for Citizen. Pawns any faceup site except Chancellor top Cradle. Chancellor Oathkeeper, gets Darkest Secret for Devotion or People’s Favor for People.
SOURCE Law 1.7–15,1.23; Playbook p30

Q024 Describe later-game discard seeding, starting adviser selection and Vision counting. Are starting Reliquary relic placements chosen or random?
KEY Seed each discard with one of three total bottom-world-deck cards; each player draws three bottom cards, then turn order chooses facedown adviser and discards other two using pawn region after placing pawn. Advance Visions Drawn for drawn Visions. Four Reliquary relics randomly one per space.
SOURCE Law 1.17–23; Errata 1.17

Q025 In first-game packet setup, which sites/pawns/garrisons/denizens/advisers are faceup or facedown, and where is Ivory Eye?
KEY Plains top Cradle,purple pawn,two purple garrison,Longbows; Mountain top Provinces,Red/Blue pawns,one purple,Taming Charm; Rocky Coast top Hinterland,Yellow pawn,one purple,Elders. Other sites facedown. Facedown advisers Chancellor Forest Paths,Red Animal Playmates,Blue Naysayers,Yellow A Small Favor. Ivory Eye facedown at Mountain. Preserve packet deck order.
SOURCE Playbook pp6–7

Q026 Can you act at a remote ruled site to Muster/Trade, use a normal Action power there, or use a battle plan at your pawn site that you do not rule? How do persistent powers differ?
KEY Muster/Trade only pawn site. Normal card power accessible by ruling card or pawn at its site, so remote ruled Action accessible. Battle plan requires rule, pawn alone insufficient. Persistent black-thick-braid power affects specified players ignoring ordinary access.
SOURCE Law 5.2–3,7.1.1,7.1.4,7.5.1

Q027 A defensive battle plan costs favor and a secret. Where do those go when used outside your turn, when is the secret ready again, and can that plan already hold resources?
KEY Favor immediately matching bank,secret stays own board facedown,cannot place/burn facedown to pay; ready at own Rest. Battle-plan payment allowed on occupied card once per Campaign. Does not allow Muster/Trade on occupied card.
SOURCE Law 7.1.2,7.5.3,4.3.2

Q028 When are ordinary action modifiers used, may the same modifier apply twice to one action or to later actions, and may an active modifier be discarded?
KEY At modified action start,in any order; each once per action, only current action. No-cost modifier can modify multiple different actions. Usually optional except must/cannot; cannot discard while modifying current action.
SOURCE Law 7.4

Q029 What is the timing order for When Played powers, how often may Wake/Rest powers happen, and may a paid power be used if it will have no effect?
KEY When Played mandatory after playing faceup,after site-favor gain,Homeland effects and modifiers. Wake once each in Wake; Rest optional once each at end Rest. May pay/use even zero effect,resolve as much as possible except may parts.
SOURCE Law 7.1.3,7.3; Errata 7.1.3

Q030 What do tree, person and chain restrictions do to faceup play/move/swap/discard, and how are two adviser-limit reductions combined and checked when played?
KEY Tree site-only,person adviser-only,also move/swap; locked cannot discard/move/swap once played except Chronicle. Restriction banners on facedown cards do not apply. Use lowest changed adviser limit,not additive; discard to satisfy new limit before playing card,not old limit. Locked cards remain protected.
SOURCE Law 7.2,7.6.4; Errata 7.6.4

Q031 Who can play Conspiracy, what exact theft conditions/cost apply, can two advisers match one enemy adviser, and where does Conspiracy end?
KEY Anyone, even Imperials. Burn one secret to take one relic or banner from any player whose pawn is at your site. Two of your own faceup advisers must each match the suit of at least one of that target player’s advisers; both may match the same adviser. The target need not be an enemy. Playing Conspiracy does not replace a revealed true Vision; banner seizure applies; Conspiracy goes to the box even if no theft is made.
SOURCE Law 5.1.4.IV; Reference p1

Q032 May you freely discard a faceup adviser, move warbands onto an empty site, or pick up the last site warband? What changes with Citizens and co-located Imperial pawns?
KEY No voluntary faceup discard unless rule prompts; no ordinary drop on empty bandit site; pick up all but last own site warband. Drop only at ruled pawn site. Citizen pickup requires Chancellor permission. Imperial pawns co-located can give/take board warbands with other player permission. Bandit Crown permits last physical pickup.
SOURCE Law 6.5,5.1.4.II,7.6.5; Playbook p32

Q033 What relics can you peek at without paying Supply, and may a relic peeked at earlier be inspected again after moving away?
KEY Any facedown relic at own pawn site; any previously peeked specific relic again from any site. Scepter holder can peek Reliquary (subject cannot use Scepter taken this turn). Other sites’ unpeeked relics require power.
SOURCE Law 6.3–4; Grand Scepter

Q034 If the Scepter holder exiles a Citizen, how is favor payment calculated, which warbands change color, and does this end the recipient’s Act?
KEY Pay five,+one for Citizen Oathkeeper,+one Citizen People’s Favor,minus one payer Oathkeeper,minus one payer People’s Favor. Flip Exile,replace board purple with own color,refresh full; map garrisons stay purple. Does not by itself end recipient Act.
SOURCE Law 6.7

Q035 How is self-exile paid, who is prohibited from doing it, what warbands change, and does Act continue?
KEY Citizen gives Scepter holder favor equal board warbands plus secrets on own board and denizen/relic/edifice cards. Scepter holder cannot self-exile. Flip Exile,replace board purple with own color,full Supply,end Act. Map purple stays.
SOURCE Law 6.8

Q036 Two players tie the current title holder; later the holder falls behind two tied leaders. Who holds title, and when is Supremacy transferred during Campaign?
KEY Current holder keeps when tied for goal. If holder no longer meets goal,chooses among tied qualifying others. New recipient Oathkeeper-side. Supremacy transfer after Campaign ends,not temporary mid-Campaign losses. Empire collective purple rule credits Chancellor.
SOURCE Law 2.11; Errata 2.11

Q037 An attack-die pool is empty and a battle plan removes an attack die. What happens? Which battle plans do bandits use and in what sequence do sides choose plans?
KEY For each removal from empty attack pool,add defense die. Attacker chooses ruled plans once each then defender; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. Plan resources do not block paying its plan cost.
SOURCE Law 5.5.3,7.5

Q038 After skulls leave an attacking force of five warbands, the attacker loses. How many die and where do survivors go? Does winning defender take attacker’s relics?
KEY Kill half remaining force rounded down:two,leaving three on attacker board. Only victorious attacker resolves declared targets; winning defender takes no attacker relics. Skulls already removed before halving.
SOURCE Law 5.5.5–7

Q039 A defender’s pawn is away from attacker and every targeted site. Do board warbands defend, and do warbands at untargeted sites defend? How are shield doubles applied?
KEY No board force unless pawn at attacker/targeted site; only targeted-site garrisons add,not untargeted sites. Doubles multiply rolled shields exponentially,not warband defense. No intrinsic warband defense dice.
SOURCE Law 5.5.4; Playbook p32

Q040 Are warbands, favor, secrets and dice component-limited? If a requested gain exceeds a source, what is done, and can you intentionally burn extra resources?
KEY Warbands/favor/cards limited; secrets/dice unlimited. Gain/take maximum possible from source,not more; boards/banks no cap unless specified. Cannot place/burn/sacrifice beyond prompted cost/requirement.
SOURCE Law 9.3,9.5

Q041 Which game information is private and public? May a holder show a facedown adviser or lie about its identity?
KEY Private facedown fronts,discard fronts,world-deck count and backs beyond top. Public all else including discard counts/backs and board favor,secrets,warbands. Holder may peek/show facedown adviser and players may lie about private info; cannot mix advisers indistinguishably.
SOURCE Law 9.4

Q042 How do must, cannot, ignore and must-if-able interact; which book takes priority; do a Give restriction and a Take restriction mean the same thing?
KEY Cannot beats must,which beats ordinary; ignore overrides specifically named must/cannot. Must-if-able fulfilled when possible,otherwise no penalty. Law beats Playbook/aids except Site Reference,nonitalic beats reminder. Give/Take distinct; restricting one does not change other.
SOURCE Law 9.1–2; Errata Glossary

Q043 Are ordinary promises or free resource gifts binding/legal? What exceptions exist, including Reliquary relics and Tribunal?
KEY Ordinary promises nonbinding; unprompted resource transfer not authorized. Citizenship and powers saying binding bind agreed listed things if able. Only Citizenship offer can exchange Reliquary relic; Tribunal binding favor/secrets and future actions,disputed breach coin flip.
SOURCE Law 6.6.1,7.6.3,9.6; Reference p2

Q044 What happens when each of the four Reliquary spaces is uncovered for Chancellor: Brutal, Decadent, Careless and Greedy?
KEY Brutal: when Chancellor attacker,defeated player even self kills all force. Decadent: travel Provinces/Hinterland→Cradle no Supply; to Hinterland +1 Supply. Careless: Trade gains one extra favor even secret trade; secret trade gains one fewer secret. Greedy: draw two extra on Search,still stops at world Vision,cannot Search if cost >2 Supply. Mandatory uncovered modifiers.
SOURCE Law setup illustration; Playbook p3 Reliquary

Q045 Which winner can build or repair an edifice in Chronicle, how many, where, and may a new edifice replace a denizen at a site already holding a ruin?
KEY Only Chancellor/Citizen winner,one build or repair. Build at ruled site with no edifice intact or ruined,replace matching denizen by intact Archive edifice,denizen to world deck. Or repair ruled ruin by flipping intact. No building over an existing ruin.
SOURCE Law 8.3.1; Playbook Chronicle aid p4

Q046 In Chronicle, which sites are discarded, where do their attached cards go, and what happens to retained sites with intact edifices not ruled by winner?
KEY Discard sites unless winner rules or intact edifice exists;shuffle sites into deck,denizens to discard,relics to relic deck,ruined edifices Archive. At retained non-winner sites flip intact edifice to ruin and discard denizens there. Set aside all ruin sites with attached ruin,denizens,relics in map order; remove all pawns/resources/warbands from map.
SOURCE Law 8.3.2–4; Errata 8.3.3

Q047 Give the ordered Chronicle process for filling empty map slots, including the reverse ordering of ruins and faceup-site guarantee.
KEY Non-ruins: fill Cradle top-down with Cradle then Provinces then Hinterland top-down; Provinces top-down push then import Hinterland; push Hinterland up. Ruins saved in top-to-bottom order then place bottom-up into Hinterland bottom-up,then Provinces bottom-up. Fill remaining slots facedown from site deck; flip top site in regions with no faceup site.
SOURCE Law 8.3.5

Q048 How are six Archive cards selected for world deck in Chronicle, including suit ties and no suited advisers?
KEY Winner most common adviser suit,choose tied suit or any if no suited advisers;three random cards of it,two next clockwise,one next. Clockwise Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord.
SOURCE Law 8.4; map favor-bank order

Q049 If Archive cannot supply the Chronicle’s required 3/2/1 cards, is a partial allocation added, and how is the Archive healed?
KEY Do not add normal allocation. Take all Dispossessed,sort six suit stacks,take six random from largest stack into world deck,shuffle each remaining Dispossessed suit stack into matching Archive stack.
SOURCE Law 8.4

Q050 What cards are eligible to become Dispossessed during Chronicle, how many are removed, and what happens to Visions and winner’s advisers?
KEY Set aside all five Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all region discards with losing players advisers;take six random unseen into Dispossessed. Winner advisers excluded from removal pool;later remaining denizens feed rebuild (site attachments remain saved).
SOURCE Law 8.5,8.8

Q051 Explain Chronicle relic cleanup order, including Grand Scepter, losing relics, site refill and winner/Reliquary relics.
KEY Grand Scepter saved World Box. Losing players relics back relic deck and shuffle. Refill each faceup site to printed R count only if below,place facedown. Shuffle winner remaining held relics with Reliquary relics and put atop relic deck. Site refill precedes winner/Reliquary stacking.
SOURCE Law 8.6

Q052 How are map cards and boards packed after Chronicle, and does the next group need the same players or status ownership?
KEY Stack attached cards on each site;stack sites top Cradle on top,bottom Hinterland bottom,save World Box. Boards saved current Exile/Citizen sides. New people can join;non-Chancellors choose among saved boards in turn order unless group agrees reservations.
SOURCE Law 8.7,1.9; Playbook p31

Q053 A matching-suit card is played to a Homeland site after a different-suit card was discarded there this turn. Does reward trigger, what can reward be, and how is a relic reward resolved?
KEY Yes provided no card of matching Homeland suit was discarded there this turn. Printed reward: favor or secret from matching bank/shared bank,or two warbands,or take site relic treating as Recover (no ordinary Recover action/site cost). Gain site-play favor then Homeland effect before When Played.
SOURCE Site Reference p2; Law 7.3.3

Q054 How do Coast sites change Travel and interact with Narrow Pass? Is it enough that destination alone is a Coast?
KEY From a Coast to another Coast costs one Supply and ignores Narrow Pass;both origin and destination required. Destination-only Coast uses normal costs/restrictions unless another effect applies.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Coasts

Q055 When does Narrow Pass require travel to itself or an added Campaign target, and does ruling Narrow Pass change those conditions?
KEY Entering its region from another region must travel to Narrow Pass. Campaign declaring any targets in that region while pawn in different region must also target Narrow Pass unless attacker rules it. The rule exception applies Campaign,not generic entry; named ignore effects can override.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Narrow Pass

Q056 What must be paid to travel to Hidden Place or declare Campaign targets there, and which site powers can override this restriction?
KEY Flip one board secret facedown;cannot travel/target there without doing so. Shrouded Wood travel ignores Hidden Place;Buried Giant ignores Narrow Pass only,not Hidden Place. Coasts ignore Narrow Pass only.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Hidden Place,Shrouded Wood,Buried Giant

Q057 From Buried Giant, how can you travel without Supply, where does the secret go, and does that automatically ignore Hidden Place?
KEY May flip one secret on own board facedown;spend no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass when traveling from there. Secret remains board exhausted,cannot pay again before refresh. Does not name/ignore Hidden Place.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Buried Giant; Law 7.1.2

Q058 How does Marshes change Search, and does it change a remote Search simply because you rule Marshes?
KEY Must draw one fewer if pawn there,so ordinary three becomes two,still stop at world Vision/empty source. Rule alone without pawn there does not trigger it.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Marshes; Law 5.1.2

Q059 When may Great Slum discard a card first, and does this allow discarding there at any unrelated time?
KEY When playing or moving a card to this site,may first discard card there,subject locks. It is a timed permission,not unrestricted discard at other times.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Great Slum; Law 7.2.2

Q060 Who chooses destination when traveling from enemy-ruled Shrouded Wood, what is its fixed cost, and does forced banishment bypass it?
KEY Fixed cost two before other Travel modifiers;ignore Narrow Pass/Hidden Place. If enemy rules it,travel to ruler choice (Chancellor for Empire),even when another player forces travel. Banishment spends no Supply but does not override destination choice.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Shrouded Wood; Law 5.5.7.III; Errata 5.6

Q061 Do Plains and Mountain modify dice only if the site itself is targeted, and does ruling the site cancel the modifier?
KEY Mandatory +one attack die Plains/−one Mountain if any targets at site,including site,even if attacker rules it. Not dependent on site being target itself.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Plains,Mountain

Q062 What additional warband does River grant, and what happens if you Muster there without ruling it?
KEY If Muster at River and rule it,gain one more warband,three total ordinary. If do not rule it,ordinary two;eligible empty card,cost still applies and finite bank limit.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 River; Law 5.2,9.3

Q063 Traveling from Charming Valley in Provinces normally costs how much Supply? What if a spend-no-Supply power is used?
KEY Base two plus one increase=three. Spend-no-Supply overrides increase,zero Supply. Fixed-number change applied before increases.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Charming Valley; Law 7.6.2; Errata 5.6

Q064 Who may use Tribunal’s Action, what immediate resources does it let players exchange, and how is a disputed future breach resolved?
KEY Its ruler or player whose pawn there may negotiate binding exchange of favor/secrets now,and future actions in combination with any player. Coin flip if unclear whether agreed future promise broken. Does not grant generic immediate exchange of relics/banners.
SOURCE Site Reference p2 Tribunal; Law 7.6.3

Q065 How does Bandit Crown affect empty sites, picking up last physical warband, defense and sacrificing bandits?
KEY Treat bandits as own warbands:rule empty faceup sites,may pick up last physical at own site,add bandits at targeted sites to defense or relevant attack with powers. Bandits cannot kill/move/sacrifice for skulls,losses,Tyrant/Cursed Cauldron.
SOURCE Law 7.6.5

Q066 Can a player rule a facedown site or put cards there using a move power? What does a ruined edifice contribute to capacity, suit and action access?
KEY No:only faceup sites ruled and facedown sites cannot hold cards. Ruin counts denizen/edifice capacity,has no suit,cannot Muster/Trade,but its power still functions per access/text.
SOURCE Law 2.8–9; Errata 2.8,Rule

Q067 Must every draw from the world deck follow the entire Search draw-stop procedure, or does the corrected Draw glossary differ? What always happens when a Vision is drawn from world deck?
KEY Corrected Draw simply takes top cards from prompted source;does not automatically import all Search rules into other powers. Always advance Visions Drawn for world-deck Vision,including Oracle. Search itself must stop at world Vision.
SOURCE Errata Draw; Law 2.7.1,5.1.2

Q068 Can you take several major/minor actions in any order, stop without spending all Supply, or begin another action before current one finishes?
KEY Any number/order/repeats including none while costs payable;may stop and preserve unspent Supply through Rest;must finish current action before next. No interrupting Campaign with another normal minor action.
SOURCE Law 4.2–3

Q069 If you seize a banner by Conspiracy or a binding transfer rather than Campaign, does it lose resources? How does Recover differ?
KEY Any taking except Recover is seizure;burn two banner favor/secrets down to minimum one,People’s Favor Mob. Recover instead replaces resources with paid outbid,distributes old as described,and People’s Favor normal. No burn-two seizure on Recover.
SOURCE Law 2.5.3,Glossary Seize,5.4

Q070 Can a Citizen’s defensive battle plan prohibit other Allies’ battle plans, and who decides contested order or competing use of a shared plan?
KEY Power references you/defender cover whole defending side,so cannot-use-other-plans limits all Allies. Your site/board remain individual. Declared defender resolves order/priority and competing shared use;one specific plan once total,user pays.
SOURCE Errata 5.5; Law 5.5.3

Q071 When a new Citizen’s conversion needs more purple warbands than available, who decides what is removed, and what is converted when that Citizen later becomes Exile?
KEY New Citizen chooses which existing board/map warbands to replace purple and which to remove for shortage. Later exile converts only board warbands to own color;map garrisons stay purple. Gain/take source shortage maximum possible.
SOURCE Law 6.6.2,6.7–8,9.3

Q072 If the People’s Favor is normal with five favor and its holder adds one at Wake, how many choices happen this Wake? What if it was already Mob?
KEY Normal begins with one choice;add sixth then final check flips Mob,no retroactive second choice. Already Mob makes two choices,each obeying last-favor restriction;does not revert just by falling below six.
SOURCE Law 4.1.1

Q073 Can an Exile holding an unrevealed true Vision win at Wake, or reveal it at Wake to win immediately? What if fewer than three world Visions have been drawn?
KEY No:must already have revealed and complete at victory check;normal reveal minor action in Act,not Wake. Fewer than three world Visions blocks Visionary even if goal assets met;may reveal earlier for future.
SOURCE Law 3.2,4.1.2,6.1

Q074 Can an Exile whose title has not yet flipped to Usurper win as Oathkeeper at end of round eight? If not, who can win instead?
KEY Oathkeeper alone not Usurper win;priority Empire-Oathkeeper absent if Exile holds,then existing Usurper,then qualifying Visionary,then Empire fallback with possible Successor. Exile can still win qualifying revealed Vision.
SOURCE Law 3.4

Q075 At Chronicle, if Exile wins through both Usurper and Vision, must next Oath match Vision? Who may receive Chronicle Citizenship and how are accepting site garrisons replaced?
KEY Multiple-method win chooses any Oath except current,not forced Vision match. Flip all Citizen boards Exile;winner may offer other Exiles except just-flipped former Citizens,not self. Accepting Exile sites replace all garrisons with one winner-color warband per ruled site;no normal Reliquary gift.
SOURCE Law 8.1–2; Errata 8.2

Q076 When playing through People’s Favor, must discarded and receiving sites be identical, can the discard come from another region, and can a locked card be discarded?
KEY Sites may differ but both must be in pawn region;cannot use power to discard elsewhere. Locked faceup card cannot be discarded. Receiving site capacity still applies;gain played-card suit favor as normal.
SOURCE Law 5.1.4.I,7.2.2

Q077 If a victorious attacker targeted pawn/favor and a banner, must they banish, must they burn favor, and must they take the banner? What is the rounding of board favor burn?
KEY Banish optional;board favor burn independently optional,half rounded down. Taking all targeted relics/banners mandatory. Seized banner burns two its resources min one separately from optional board-favor burn.
SOURCE Law 5.5.7

Q078 What do skulls do if you chose fewer attack dice than board warbands, and can you sacrifice more than required to win to reduce your upkeep?
KEY Each skull kills own force warband immediately,not one per rolled die necessarily nor defender. Choice of fewer dice does not shrink force to those dice for casualties. Sacrifice exactly necessary to win if choose,never surplus to adjust upkeep.
SOURCE Law 5.5.2,5.5.5–6,9.5

Q079 What does the Exile/Chancellor Supply refresh depend on exactly, and how much Supply do their personal-bank brackets give before saving?
KEY Unused personal-bank warbands,not board/map. Chancellor 18+:6,11–17:5,4–10:4,0–3:3. Exile9+:6,4–8:5,0–3:4. Add saved remaining Supply capped at full seven. Citizen instead exact Chancellor marker.
SOURCE Law 4.3.3–4; player boards Playbook p3

Q080 Which battle-plan box colors can attacker and defender use? Does rule alone permit a side to use the wrong-color plan?
KEY Red attacker only,blue defender only,gradient either. Must rule and meet color/role permission;rule alone insufficient.
SOURCE Law 7.5 introductory paragraph

Q081 For Chancellor/Citizen versus Exile, who is an enemy? How does an intra-Empire Campaign and the phrase your enemy change that?
KEY Ordinary Imperials enemies are Exiles;Exiles enemies any other player. Specified Citizen temporarily non-Imperial during intra-Empire Campaign considers others enemies. Bandits enemies everyone and vice versa. Your enemy means opposing Campaign side: defender+Allies for attacker,attacker for defender.
SOURCE Law Glossary Enemy,Your Enemy; Errata Enemy/You

Q082 May Search voluntarily draw only one of three available cards when no Vision or reducing modifier intervenes? What if source runs out?
KEY No;draw prescribed three unless world Vision stops,source exhausted,or applicable modifier changes count. Empty source means take only available,no automatic reshuffle.
SOURCE Law 5.1.2; Playbook p32

Q083 At setup, where do the Round and Visions Drawn markers start? Who takes the first turn of every round, in which direction does play proceed, what phases make a turn, and when is an end-of-round victory check made relative to moving the round marker?
KEY Both markers start on their first/star spaces (Round1 and Visions Drawn0). Starting with the Chancellor each round, go clockwise with one turn per player. Each turn is Wake, Act, Rest in that order. After every player has taken a turn, the round ends: check the applicable end-of-round victory condition before advancing the round marker; round8 ends automatically.
SOURCE Law 1.2; Law 4 introductory paragraph; Law 3.3–4; Playbook p6 step5; Playbook p10

Q084 During the first-game packet setup, do players make the later-game bottom-deck adviser draws or shuffle the ordered packet world deck? How are the regional discards and the Reliquary/relic deck prepared?
KEY Use the assigned facedown advisers instead of later-game adviser draws. Put three facedown cards in the Cradle discard, three in the Provinces discard and five in the Hinterland discard. Put the remaining41 denizen/Vision cards on the World Deck space in Packet B order. Give the Chancellor the Grand Scepter, put Ivory Eye facedown at Mountain, put the next four relic cards facedown in the four Reliquary spaces, and the remaining15 on the Relic Deck space. Preserve the packet instructions/order rather than replacing this with later setup’s bottom draws and random preparation.
SOURCE Playbook p7 steps12–18; Playbook p6–7 first-game setup; Law 1 introductory first-time exception

Q085 Before resolving the first game’s Chronicle, how must the unopened Archive Packet be prepared?
KEY Open the Archive Packet. Put the eight cardboard separators in the small box compartment. Put the six edifices in their matching-suit sections. Shuffle each of the six suit stacks separately and put each stack in its matching section; this forms the Archive. Then use the Chronicle aid and Law8 to pack/save the game.
SOURCE Playbook p29 Ending Your First Game

Q086 If a power lets an Exile become a Citizen with no offer, is a Grand Scepter offer or exactly one Reliquary relic still required, and which status-conversion consequences still apply?
KEY No. Forced Citizenship follows the power and the acceptance/conversion procedure in6.6.2 without requiring the ordinary offer in6.6.1 or its promised Reliquary relic. Flip the board to Citizen, replace board/map warbands with available purple warbands with the Exile choosing shortage removals/replacements, discard a revealed Vision, flip a held Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end Act if it is their turn, and refresh Supply to the leftmost space. Do not invent an ordinary promised exchange when there was no offer.
SOURCE Law 7.6.1; Law 6.6.1–2

Q087 A normal Action/modifier card already holds favor or a secret. May you place another favor/secret on it to pay for its power? May its power still be used if it has no cost, and what special case changes the payment rule?
KEY Normally you cannot place favor or secrets on a card that already has either, so you cannot pay such a placement cost. Occupancy does not prevent using a power that has no cost. Battle plans specifically allow placing payment on an occupied card, while still being usable only once per Campaign; this does not permit Muster or Trade on an occupied card.
SOURCE Law 7.1.2; Law 7.5.3; Card Reference p1 Rules of Use: Exhaustion; Playbook p32 Using Cards

Q088 What mandatory defense-die bonus does the Oathkeeper title give on its Oathkeeper side versus its Usurper side? Is this a Campaign modifier, and how does Supremacy apply it to Imperial defense?
KEY The Oathkeeper must add one defense die; the Usurper must add two. The title bonus is a Campaign modifier. For Supremacy the Chancellor holds the title if the Empire meets the goal and always adds its power when any Imperial player defends. Apply the errata’s side-sharing permissions to participating Imperial defenders/Allies in other Oaths as well.
SOURCE Law 2.11; Errata Law Clarifications2.11; Errata Campaign power-sharing

Q089 A power says to move or swap a denizen rather than play it. Must this obey site/adviser capacities and tree/person/locked restrictions? Does the movement by itself award the favor for playing to a site or trigger a When Played power?
KEY Move follows capacity, play-placement and restriction rules (2.8.1,5.1.4,7.2); Swap moves both prompted pieces to each other’s locations and also follows those movement rules. A move/swap is not itself a play, so it does not by itself award the favor for playing to a site or trigger When Played. A power explicitly saying to play follows the Play rules and those triggers.
SOURCE Law Glossary Move,Swap,Play; Law 9.1 literal interpretation; Law 5.1.4.I; Law 7.3.3

Q090 When a Citizen’s purple warband is killed by a skull, sacrifice, or Campaign loss, which bank receives it? How does this differ from moving a defeated force’s surviving warbands?
KEY Kill moves a warband to the personal bank of the player of that color: purple goes to the Chancellor’s personal bank even when killed from a Citizen’s board. Sacrifice means choosing to kill one’s own warband. Defeated survivors move to a board rather than to a personal bank; in Imperial defense surviving site warbands go to the Chancellor’s board and survivors already on Citizen boards stay there.
SOURCE Law Glossary Kill,Sacrifice; Law 5.5.5–6; Law 5.5.7.I Empire box as relocated by errata

Q091 Bandits rule more faceup sites than any player. Do they compete for the Oathkeeper or Vision goals or prevent a player from having the most sites among players?
KEY No. Bandits act as a neutral defender for Campaign purposes and rule empty faceup sites, but they do not compete for victory goals. Compare the relevant players, not bandits, when resolving those goals.
SOURCE Playbook p32 Campaigns; Law Glossary Rule as corrected by errata; Law 2.11; Law 3.2

Q092 At Salt Flats, Mine or Drowned City, when and from where may a player take income? Can they take both one favor and one secret, use a remotely ruled site, or take from a bank if that site is empty?
KEY At the end of Wake, after the People’s Favor procedure, Exile win check and title flip, a player whose pawn is at the eligible site may take one favor or one secret from that site. It is one token total, not one of each; remote rule alone does not qualify, and an empty site supplies nothing rather than a substitute token from a bank.
SOURCE Law 4.1.1–4; Site Reference p2 Opportunity Sites; Law 9.3

Q093 The attacker loses a Campaign. The defender used a battle plan saying “If you're victorious,” and both players used plans saying “At end, discard [card name].” What resolves after the roll, in what order, and does losing let the attacker keep their end-discard plan?
KEY Resolve the defeated attacker's losses first: kill half of the warbands remaining in their force, rounded down, keep the survivors on their board, then resolve any battle plans they used that say “If you're defeated.” Skip the attacker's target-taking step because the attacker lost. In Step 8, resolve the victorious defender's “If you're victorious” battle plans. Then discard the applicable “At end, discard [card name]” plans used by either player. The defeated attacker still discards such a plan; the end-discard instruction does not require its user to have won. Apply the text of each effect, including any optional parts.
SOURCE Law 5.5.6 Resolve Defeat, printed p7; Law 5.5.7 Resolve Attacker's Victory, printed p7; Law 5.5.8 Resolve Battle Plans, printed p7; Law 7.1.3 Use (resolve as much as possible except may parts), printed p9

Q094 A battle plan you rule has a gradient power box and a ± attack-die symbol. Must an attacker add the die and a defender remove it, or may either user choose either sign? Does ± also let you change defense dice?
KEY Either the attacker or defender may use a gradient battle plan and choose to add or remove the attack die shown. The plus/minus symbol means add or remove the type of die shown; it does not switch an attack-die effect into a defense-die effect, and the user’s role does not choose the sign. Normal battle-plan access, payment and once-per-Campaign rules still apply.
SOURCE Law 7.5.4 Iconography, printed p9: battle plans with a +/– symbol can add or remove the type of die shown.; Law 7.5 introductory paragraph, printed p9: gradient boxes allow attacker or defender.; Law 7.5.1–3, printed p9: rule/access, use timing, payment and use limit.; Card Reference p1 Common Icons: Add or remove symbol.

Q095 You have a faceup card effect beginning “Wake:” whose text contains no “may”. May you choose to skip it because it would be inconvenient, just as you can decline a “Rest:” power? Is taking Opportunity-site income at Wake compulsory too?
KEY No. Wake powers happen during your Wake Phase, once each; you do not have a general option to skip such a Wake effect. Resolve as much of its effect as possible, respecting its conditions and other restrictions, except any parts that explicitly say “may”. Rest powers are optional and may be used once each at the end of Rest. Taking one favor or secret at Salt Flats, Mine or Drowned City is explicitly optional, so you may decline that income.
SOURCE Law7.3.1 Wake, printed p9: Wake powers happen once each during Wake; the reminder distinguishes mandatory powers from optional taking of site favor/secrets.; Law7.3.4 Rest and Law4.3.5, printed pp9,5: Rest powers may be used once each at end of Rest.; Law7.1.3 Use, printed p9: must resolve as much as possible except parts saying may.; Law4.1.4 Use Site Power, printed p5; Site Reference p2 Opportunity Sites: may take one favor or secret.

Q096 A Red Exile’s pawn is at a faceup site garrisoned by purple warbands, while red warbands occupy a different faceup site without their pawn. Which site and its denizen cards does Red rule? Does moving the pawn by itself change rule, and can red and purple site warbands coexist to share rule of one site?
KEY Red rules the faceup site containing their red warbands and the cards at that site, even though their pawn is elsewhere. Red does not rule the purple-garrisoned site merely because their pawn is there. A player also rules their own advisers. Moving a pawn by itself does not move the site warbands or change this basis of rule. A site can hold warbands of only one color at a time; different colors do not share a site by coexisting there. Imperial players share rule of purple-garrisoned sites under the Empire exception, rather than by placing different colors together.
SOURCE Law 10, Rule, corrected by errata to faceup sites; Law 6.6.3 Imperial Players; Playbook p8, Ruling Sites on the Map; Playbook p18: pawns do not matter for rule

Q097 A power tells you to reveal a facedown card, without telling you to play it. Who sees its front? Is this the same instruction as peeking, and does revealing alone award favor for site play or trigger a When Played power?
KEY Reveal means show the card’s front to everyone. Peek means the prompted player looks at its front. Revealing alone is not an instruction to Play: it does not itself put a card at a site, in advisers, or in a personal bank. Therefore the reveal alone does not grant the favor for playing to a site or trigger a When Played power. If the effect separately instructs you to play the card, follow that instruction and the ordinary play restrictions and triggers.
SOURCE Law 10, Reveal, Peek, Play; Law 9.1 literal interpretation; Law 5.1.4.I gain for playing to site; Law 7.3.3 When Played

Q098 While resolving a power, an instruction says to do something “after” a specified event. May you postpone that instruction until after an intervening step of the same action? What exact timing does “after” prescribe?
KEY No. After means immediately following: nothing happens between the specified event and the prompted instruction. It does not provide a discretionary later window within the action. Follow any explicit text governing the actual effect; this definition does not invent a priority rule for simultaneous effects.
SOURCE Law 10, After; Law 9.1 literal interpretation

Q099 Unless an effect specifies different locations, where do favor/secrets, an adviser card, and a relic move when you Take them? How does Give reverse the direction? If a power simply tells you to Burn a favor or secret, can you choose a token on a banner or card instead of your board, and where does it go?
KEY Take moves the prompted favor or secrets from the prompted player’s board to your board, a card from their advisers to your advisers, or a relic from their personal bank—or the prompted site or draw source—to your personal bank. Give is the reverse direction of Take. Burn normally moves the prompted favor or secret from your own board to the shared bank; another location is used only if the effect prompts it. A plain Burn instruction does not let you substitute a token from a banner or card. Follow the actual prompt and applicable placement/restriction rules.
SOURCE Law 10, Take, Give, Burn; Law 9.1 literal interpretation

Q100 A power permits an Exchange with a prompted player, without adding a must instruction or a binding agreement. What permission does Exchange give each player? Does the word alone require both players to transfer equal amounts in a simultaneous swap?
KEY Exchange means you may Give to the prompted player and vice versa: each player has the stated permission to Give to the other. The word by itself does not impose a compulsory, equal-amount, simultaneous exchange. The actual power still controls which pieces and amounts are permitted, and any explicit binding promise or other instruction must be followed. Swap is a different instruction that moves the two prompted pieces to each other’s locations.
SOURCE Law 10, Exchange, Give, Take, Swap; Law 9.1 literal interpretation; Law 7.6.3 and 9.6 for the separate binding-promise rule
"}

Q001: An Exile who takes Oathkeeper during Act cannot win at the next Wake: the Usurper check occurs before the title flips. Q002: Oath of Supremacy matches Vision of Conquest (rule the most sites); Oath of the People matches Vision of Rebellion (hold People's Favor); Oath of Protection matches Vision of Sanctuary (hold the most relics and banners combined); Oath of Devotion matches Vision of Faith (hold Darkest Secret). Q005: The Citizen Successor goals are: Supremacy—hold more relics and banners combined than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; People—hold Darkest Secret; Protection—hold People's Favor; Devotion—hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by a true Vision or by becoming Usurper.
Q006: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, either put 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 favor from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Never remove its last favor: if it has 1, you must add if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After the choice(s), if it has 6+ favor, flip it to Mob. Becoming Mob at this last step does not cause another payment that Wake.
Q007: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; (3) refresh Supply—Exile/Chancellor based on warbands remaining in personal bank, while Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost; (4) save unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply); (5) optional Rest powers, each once in chosen order. Supply refresh values: Chancellor 18+ = 6, 11–17 = 5, 4–10 = 4, 0–3 = 3; Exile 9+ = 6, 4–8 = 5, 0–3 = 4.
Q008: Search costs 2–4 Supply and uses either the world deck or your pawn's region discard pile, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2. World-deck Search costs 2 with zero Visions drawn, 3 with 1–2, and 4 with 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces the world-deck cost with 2, with other modifiers still applying. A Vision drawn from the world deck is announced as a Vision (not necessarily named), immediately stops the draw, and advances Visions Drawn by 1. Drawing a Vision from a discard pile neither stops drawing nor advances the track.
Q009: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle, ordering multiple discards as you choose. For cards from hand/advisers, use the pile based on your pawn's region: Cradle pawn → Provinces pile; Provinces → Hinterland; Hinterland → Cradle; never the same-region pile. When discarding a card at a site in another region, apply the cycle to that card's region, not your pawn's. Favor on discarded cards immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
Q010: You may have up to 3 advisers total, faceup and facedown together. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser as permitted, respecting locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, check against the new limit before playing it and use the lowest of multiple limits. Q013: To recover Darkest Secret from another player, their pawn's site must contain at least one suited card whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. Q014: Choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender; if no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may also target any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map (one defense die each). Q017: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. The defending side shares relevant powers/modifiers; Chancellor's Oathkeeper defense bonus is shared even outside Supremacy. Q018: Base Supply costs by origin and destination region are: from Cradle to Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces to Cradle 2, Provinces 2, Hinterland 2; from Hinterland to Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. Reveal a facedown destination and place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and printed number of facedown relics from the relic deck. Apply the fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. Free Travel is the final override: a power saying spend no Supply makes the cost zero even if another power increases it, including banishment. Site-entry restrictions remain unless ignored by the named rule/power.
Q019: In play, the Grand Scepter holder cannot make an offer on the turn they took it. On a later turn, the holder—even an Exile—may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself. Q020: In the Chronicle, a victory by Vision alone sets the next Oath to match that Vision. The Chronicle aid's “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; the correct top stack is 10 + 2 = 12.

The four Oath names are **Supremacy, People, Protection, Devotion**. One Oath is active in a game. Its criterion determines who holds the title:

| Oath | Oathkeeper criterion |
|---|---|
| Supremacy | Rule the most sites |
| People | Hold People's Favor |

The four true Vision names are **Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith**. Their correspondence is:

- **Vision of Conquest** matches **Oath of Supremacy**: rule the most sites.
- **Vision of Rebellion** matches **Oath of the People**: hold People's Favor.
- **Vision of Sanctuary** matches **Oath of Protection**: hold the most relics and banners combined.
- **Vision of Faith** matches **Oath of Devotion**: hold Darkest Secret.

**Visionary victory:** Exile must have true Vision revealed and goal completed at Wake, with **at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck by all players combined**. This is a shared global count, not a requirement for that Exile to draw three personally. Can reveal it earlier but cannot win early. For Conquest/Sanctuary “most” means **strictly more than every other player**, no ties. Compare to Empire's shared rule for sites. Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.

1. Return favor on denizens/edifices to suit-matching banks.

Draw 3 cards, taking fewer only if the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces the draw. You cannot voluntarily stop early. ### Citizenship and exile during play

**Grand Scepter:** cannot use its powers the turn you took it. Its holder, even an Exile, may offer Citizenship to any Exile **including themself**, or exile another Citizen. Reliquary relics cannot be campaigned/recovered, their powers cannot be used, and they do not count toward goals while there.

**Offer:** the Grand Scepter cannot make an offer on the turn its current holder took it. In later turns it may offer any Exile, including itself. Must promise **exactly one Reliquary relic**; may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners and non-Reliquary relics. May let recipient peek at Reliquary relics. Other binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics.

**Acceptance:** flip to Citizen; replace all own warbands on board/map with purple. If insufficient purple, new Citizen chooses which to remove and which to replace. Discard revealed Vision, flip own Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, and refresh to full leftmost Supply. Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered **mandatory** Reliquary modifier. **Forced Citizenship** powers apply the same status-conversion steps without a negotiated offer: no required Scepter offer or Reliquary relic gift, and no invented promised exchange. Only an actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier. All Imperials rule purple sites; Citizenship does not itself grant a separate shared victory.

**Uncovered Reliquary modifiers, mandatory for Chancellor:** Brutal makes the defeated player kill their entire force when Chancellor attacks, even if Chancellor loses. Decadent makes Provinces/Hinterland-to-Cradle Travel cost no Supply, but Travel to Hinterland costs +1. Careless gives 1 additional favor on every Trade, even when trading for secrets, but 1 fewer secret when trading for secrets. Greedy draws 2 additional Search cards (still stopping at a world Vision) but prohibits Search costing more than 2 Supply.

**Exile another Citizen:** Scepter holder pays them 5 favor, +1 if recipient is Oathkeeper, +1 if recipient holds People's Favor, −1 if payer is Oathkeeper, −1 if payer holds People's Favor (range 3–7). Recipient flips Exile, replaces **board** purple warbands with own color and refreshes full. Purple map garrisons stay Imperial. This does not end their Act by itself.

**Self-exile:** Citizen who does not hold Scepter may give its holder favor equal to own board warbands **plus all their secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards**. ## Overview

One player is the Chancellor; the others are Exiles or Citizens. Players compete for a changing Oath, personal Visions, or succession to the Chancellor. One player wins alone. After victory, the winner writes the Chronicle, preserving a changed map, population of cards, and political order for the next game. New players can join later games.

This summary covers the complete multiplayer base game, first-game and later-game setup, and Chronicle. It incorporates the official first-printing clarifications, particularly the corrected Darkest Secret recovery restriction and Imperial defense sharing. It excludes the Clockwork Prince and New Foundations. The Law governs over the Playbook and aids except the Site Reference; printed card powers and the rules hierarchy below apply.

## Components

Map with Cradle (2 sites), Provinces (3), Hinterland (3), a facedown discard pile per region, six suit favor banks, round track, Visions Drawn track, world deck and relic deck. The game contains 23 sites, 198 denizens, 5 Visions (4 true Visions and the Conspiracy), 6 double-sided edifices, 20 relics plus the Grand Scepter, 2 banners, 4 goal references, Chancellor board, 5 Exile/Citizen boards, Imperial Reliquary, 6 pawns, 94 warbands (24 purple; 14 in each other color), 36 favor, 20 secret tokens, 10 attack dice, 6 defense dice, an end die, markers and aids. The Archive holds denizens by suit and the Dispossessed; the World Box saves the map and goal.

Your **board** holds resources and your mobile warband force. Your **personal bank** beside it holds unused warbands and held relics/banners. Your **advisers** are up to three cards to its right, counting both faceup and facedown. A revealed true Vision occupies an Exile's separate Revealed Vision space and does not use an adviser slot.

A player's pawn determines **your site** and **your region**. A pawn does not rule a site, and warbands on your board do not garrison its site. Even one of your warbands physically on a faceup site is sufficient to rule it, regardless of where your pawn is. You rule each faceup site containing your warbands, the cards at those sites, and your advisers. Sites hold only one color of warbands. All Imperial players rule every purple-garrisoned site. Bandits rule faceup sites without physical warbands; they are enemies to all players and do not compete for victory. Facedown sites cannot hold cards or be ruled.

Denizen suits are Discord, Arcane, Order, Hearth, Beast, Nomad, in that clockwise favor-bank order. A site shows its denizen/edifice card capacity, reveal prompt, relic Recover cost and special power. Both intact and ruined edifices use capacity; a ruin has no suit and cannot be used for Muster or Trade. Relics beside sites do not use their denizen/edifice capacity.

## Setup

### First game: preserve the packet order

Use packets A, B and C and the Playbook's setup, preferably with four players (Chancellor, then Red, Blue, Yellow clockwise). Do not shuffle the prepared first-game decks. The packet-based one-round walkthrough is optional teaching guidance; play afterwards uses the full rules here.

1. Lay out the map. Put Plains faceup in top Cradle slot, Mountain faceup in top Provinces slot, Rocky Coast faceup in top Hinterland slot. Place the other five packet sites facedown in their marked order: Lush Coast in the other Cradle slot, Wastes in middle Hinterland, Salt Flats in bottom Provinces; preserve the other packet placements.
2. Put purple pawn on Plains, Red and Blue on Mountain, Yellow on Rocky Coast. Place 2 purple warbands on Plains and 1 each on Mountain and Rocky Coast.
3. Start round and Visions Drawn markers on their starred spaces (round 1, zero Visions). Use Oathkeeper of Supremacy. Place banners in shared bank, People's Favor normal side with 1 favor, Darkest Secret with 1 secret. Put 3 favor in each suit bank; collect remaining favor, secrets and dice in shared bank.
4. Chancellor takes Chancellor board, Reliquary and Grand Scepter, 3 purple warbands on board and 17 in personal bank (4 are already on map), 2 favor and 1 secret on board, full leftmost Supply, and Oathkeeper title. Each Exile has 3 of their 14 warbands on board, 11 in personal bank, 1 favor, 1 secret, and full Supply.
5. Place Longbows on Plains, Taming Charm on Mountain, Elders on Rocky Coast. Seed Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland discard piles with 3/3/5 cards from the ordered packet. Give facedown advisers: Chancellor Forest Paths; Red Anim

al Playmates; Blue Naysayers; Yellow A Small Favor. Put remaining 41 denizen/Vision cards from packet B, still ordered, in world deck.
6. Place Ivory Eye facedown at Mountain, next 4 packet relics facedown on Reliquary spaces, remaining 15 in relic deck. Begin Chancellor's turn. The four-player walkthrough can be followed with three people by one person handling two colors; after the walkthrough remove one Exile color's pieces and discard their cards to continue with three.

### Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)

1. Deal saved sites with attached denizens, edifices and relics to map slots: Cradle fully, then Provinces, then Hinterland, top to bottom. Start round 1 and Visions Drawn 0; use saved goal reference.
2. Collect shared pieces and both banners. People's Favor begins normal side with 1 favor; Darkest Secret has 1 secret. Put **3 favor per suit bank**, or **4 each with 5–6 players**.
3. Choose Chancellor (previous winner recommended), seated at Cradle, others randomly. Chancellor takes purple pieces, board, Reliquary and Grand Scepter. Other players in turn order choose a board on its saved Exile or Citizen side and corresponding color's pieces. Starting Citizens receive no Reliquary relic.
4. All start at full leftmost Supply. Chancellor has 2 favor, 1 secret and 3 purple warbands on board; place 2 purple warbands on topmost faceup Cradle site and 1 at each other faceup site with a denizen or intact edifice. Chancellor begins as Oathkeeper; additionally takes Darkest Secret for Devotion or People's Favor for People.
5. Each Exile/Citizen has 1 favor and 1 secret on board; Exiles have 3 own-color board warbands, Citizens 3 purple board warbands. Resolve printed site favor/secret setup prompts from shared bank; if insufficient favor Chancellor chooses allocation. Existing Chronicled site relics stay with sites.
6. Draw 4 relics and place them randomly, one facedown on each Reliquary space; put remaining relics in relic deck.
7. If world deck was not rebuilt during previous Chronicle, first form its top 12 cards from **10 denizens plus 2 random Visions**, its next 18 from **15 denizens plus remaining 3 Visions**, and remaining denizens below. Otherwise keep the saved rebuilt deck.
8. Take 3 total cards from bottom of world deck, one per region discard. Each player in turn order draws 3 from bottom of world deck. Advance Visions Drawn for any Visions drawn. Starting Chancellor, each player places pawn on any faceup site (Chancellor must choose top Cradle site), chooses 1 drawn card as facedown adviser, and discards other 2 using normal regional destinations. Put remaining world deck on map.

## Turn Structure

Play clockwise from Chancellor, one turn each per round, for at most eight rounds. Each turn is **Wake → Act → Rest**. After everyone has acted, check round-end victory and advance round marker if play continues.

### Wake: mandatory order

1. **People's Favor**, if held: either put 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Never remove its last favor: at 1, you must add if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If banner is already Mob-side, repeat this choice once. Afterwards, if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob. A banner becoming Mob at this last step does not retroactively repeat the payment that Wake.

Greedy draws 2 additional Search cards (still stopping at a world Vision) but prohibits Search costing more than 2 Supply.

**Exile another Citizen:** Scepter holder pays them 5 favor, +1 if recipient is Oathkeeper, +1 if recipient holds People's Favor, −1 if payer is Oathkeeper, −1 if payer holds People's Favor (range 3–7). Recipient flips Exile, replaces **board** purple warbands with own color and refreshes full. Purple map garrisons stay Imperial. This does not end their Act by itself.

**Self-exile:** Citizen who does not hold Scepter may give its holder favor equal to own board warbands **plus all their secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards**. Flip Exile, replace board warbands with own color, refresh full, and **end Act**. Cannot self-exile while holding Scepter. Map garrisons stay purple.

## Scoring / Victory Conditions

### Oathkeeper title and four Oaths

The four Oath names are **Supremacy, People, Protection, Devotion**. One Oath is active in a game. Its criterion determines who holds the title:

| Oath | Oathkeeper criterion |
|---|---|
| Supremacy | Rule the most sites |
| People | Hold People's Favor |
| Protection | Hold the most relics and banners combined |
| Devotion | Hold Darkest Secret |

The four true Vision names are **Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith**. Their correspondence is:

- **Vision of Conquest** matches **Oath of Supremacy**: rule the most sites.
- **Vision of Rebellion** matches **Oath of the People**: hold People's Favor.
- **Vision of Sanctuary** matches **Oath of Protection**: hold the most relics and banners combined.
- **Vision of Faith** matches **Oath of Devotion**: hold Darkest Secret.

### Citizen succession is a separate test

A Citizen wins only by replacing a Chancellor victory with a Successor win. Use the current Oath to select this separate criterion:

| Current Oath | Citizen's Successor goal |
|---|---|
| Supremacy | Hold more relics and banners combined than the Chancellor **and every other Citizen** |
| People | Hold Darkest Secret |
| Protection | Hold People's Favor |
| Devotion | Hold Grand Scepter |

A Citizen does not use the Oathkeeper criterion or a Vision goal as their Successor goal. Meeting the Successor criterion alone never ends the game; it matters when the Chancellor would win.

### Title transfer and victory timing

Current holder keeps title on a tie for its goal. If holder no longer meets goal and several others tie for it, outgoing holder chooses recipient. A new holder always takes it Oathkeeper-side, never Usurper-side. Under Supremacy Chancellor holds it if Empire collectively meets goal; Citizens do not count purple sites separately against each other. Other Oaths concern personal holdings. The Grand Scepter counts as a relic when held; Reliquary relics do not.

**Usurper victory has two timing windows:** at the start of an Exile's turn during Wake, or at the end of round 8 under the endgame priority. From taking Oathkeeper during Act, the normal sequence is next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake **or at the end of round 8 if that arrives first while still Usurper**. Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence. A title still on Oathkeeper at game end is insufficient.

**Visionary victory:** Exile must have true Vision revealed and goal completed at Wake, with **at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck by all players combined**. This is a shared global count, not a requirement for that Exile to draw three personally. Can reveal it earlier but cannot win early. For Conquest/Sanctuary “most” means **strictly more than every other player**, no ties. Compare to Empire's shared rule for sites. Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.

**Stable regime:** at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll end die only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper. Ends on respectively **6 / 5–6 / 3–6**. Chancellor wins, except a Citizen meeting Successor goal wins **alone instead**. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.

**War exhaustion:** round 8 ends automatically. Check in this exact priority:

1. If Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper: Empire wins (Chancellor unless qualified Successor).
2. Otherwise, Exile Usurper wins.
3. Otherwise, qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins. If several qualify, priority **Conquest → Rebellion → Sanctuary → Faith**.
4. Otherwise Empire wins (Chancellor unless qualified Successor), even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.

Holding Successor goal never ends game on its own. Resolve it whenever Chancellor would win. After victory, write Chronicle below.

Access a card's power if you rule it or your pawn is at its site; relic holders use held relics. Persistent powers (thick black braid) affect the players specified regardless of ordinary access. Sites specify their own use conditions. Chancellor must apply uncovered Reliquary modifiers; title holder must apply title power.
